stunts.name: Acrobat
stunts.text: You are able to perform impressive acrobatic feats. No individual source of opposition related to balance can be used to justify opposition to your actions.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.5.1

stunts.name: By My Hand, Set the World in Motion
stunts.text: Through a combination of speed, dexterity, and uncanny timing, you always have a path forward. In a static environment, this means that you are capable of crazy parkour-like movement to get almost anywhere that could be physically accessed. In a more fluid environment you are impossible to pin down or fence in, as you’ll always find the gap.

stunts.name: Hardcore Parkour
stunts.text: +2 to overcome actions with Athletics if you are in a chase across rooftops or a similarly precarious environment.

stunts.name: Human Spider
stunts.text: +2 to overcome or create advantage actions with Athletics on any climb.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.5.3

stunts.name: Mountaineer
stunts.text: +2 to overcome with Athletics when faced with mountainous terrain.

stunts.name: Pole Balance
stunts.text: +2 to overcome or defend with Athletics when you need to balance and have a pole in hand.

stunts.name: Rigging Rat
stunts.text: +2 to overcome with Athletics when climbing on board a ship.

stunts.name: Sea Legs
stunts.text: Your Athletics skill works unimpeded by conditions like storms, water, or high seas while on board a ship.

stunts.name: Acrobatic Dodge
stunts.text: +2 to overcome with Athletics when another character presents an obstacle to you moving between zones.

stunts.name: The Drunkard Stumbles
stunts.text: You stagger and stumble without control, but your enemy always seems to miss you and strike a nearby obstacle, causing damage to themselves. When you dodge a blow with Athletics, your opponent takes one stress, or two stress if you succeed with style.

stunts.name: Dazing Counter
stunts.text: When you succeed with style on a defend action against an opponent’s Fight roll, you automatically counter with some sort of nerve punch or stunning blow. You get to attach the Dazed situation aspect to your opponent with a free invoke, instead of just a boost.

stunts.name: The Drunkard’s Stagger
stunts.text: You sway and stagger on your feet, evading enemy blows seemingly by chance. When you succeed in a defensive Athletics roll using this technique, you gain +1 on your next attack against the opponent who tried to hit you. If you succeed with style, gain +2.

stunts.name: Evasion
stunts.text: You have an amazing ability to remain unharmed when caught within the blast radius of an explosion. +2 to defend with Athletics against area attacks.

stunts.name: The Falling Drunkard
stunts.text: When an enemy attacks, you lose your balance and fall to the ground, rolling back to your feet quickly, but your enemy now finds himself dangerously overextended. Roll Athletics to dodge. On a success, place a boost on your opponent such as Overextended or Off-Balance that anyone may use against him. On a success with style, place a second boost on your opponent.

stunts.name: Favored Enemy Dodge
stunts.text: Choose an organisation. You gain +2 to defend with Athletics against members of that group.

stunts.name: Lightning Reflexes
stunts.text: +2 to defend with Athletics for the first exchange after you become aware of a threat.

stunts.name: Protector
stunts.text: You are an expert bodyguard. +2 to defend with Athletics whenever you pull someone out of harm's way at great personal risk to yourself.

stunts.name: Reading the Line of Fire
stunts.text: You can tell where the bullets will go before the trigger is pulled. +2 to Athletics when using it to dodge gunfire.

stunts.name: Redirect Attack
stunts.text: Once per scene, when you succeed with style on a defence roll with Athletics against Fight, you may force your opponent to attack another of your enemies in the same zone with the same attack roll.

stunts.name: Slippery
stunts.text: +2 when using Athletics to defend against or overcome knockbacks and pushes.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.5.1

stunts.name: War Mount
stunts.text: You work together with your rider to defend yourselves. +2 to defend with Athletics while being ridden.

stunts.name: Safe Fall
stunts.text: You can skip effortlessly down sheer surfaces. Whenever you fail an Athletics roll and fall vertically near a solid surface, reduce the stress you take by 2.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.5.1

stunts.name: Land On Your Feet
stunts.text: Like a cat, you are able to fall from great heights without excessive harm. When making an Athletics roll to resist falling damage, add +2 to the roll.

stunts.name: Fight By Jumping
stunts.text: It is normally a very bad idea to jump up high while fighting, but you make it work. +2 to Athletics when creating a jump-based advantage in combat, but all aspects created this way disappear at the end of your next turn.

stunts.name: Long Jump
stunts.text: +2 to Athletics when jumping significant distances horizontally.

stunts.name: Mighty Leap/Spring-Heeled
stunts.text: Your leaping ability borders on the superhuman. +2 to overcome with Athletics whenever height is a major factor.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.5.3

stunts.name: Out of Reach
stunts.text: It isn't easy to hit a guy who's five feet above your head. When you create an aspect using Fight By Jumping, you may move into the zone above your current zone as a free action, provided there are no situation aspects restricting that movement.

stunts.name: Vault
stunts.text: +2 to overcome with Athletics when you have a long pole in hand and the obstacle is primarily height-based.

stunts.name: The Bastard Will Not Escape
stunts.text: Nobody gets away from you. +2 to overcome with Athletics when chasing someone on foot.

stunts.name: Fast as a Leopard
stunts.text: You are incredibly fast on your feet. +2 to create advantage or overcome actions with Athletics used to move multiple zones on the flat.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.5.2

stunts.name: Faster than a Leopard
stunts.text: You are simply, astonishingly fast. When you move multiple zones in a straight line, you get an additional +2 to create advantage or overcome actions with Athletics.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.5.2

stunts.name: Run Away!
stunts.text: Discretion is the better part of valour, at least for you. On a successful defence with Athletics, you may sacrifice your next action to immediately flee, making an overcome action with Athletics and using your total on the defence roll as your total on the overcome roll.

stunts.name: Sprinter/Highly Mobile
stunts.text: You move two zones for free in a conflict without rolling, instead of one, provided there are no situation aspects restricting movement.

stunts.name: Contortionist
stunts.text: If you choose to spend an action moving from one zone to an adjacent one, your Athletics skill works unimpeded by conditions such as narrow openings, low ceilings, or other cramped conditions.

stunts.name: Escapologist
stunts.text: +2 to overcome actions with Athletics when escaping from bonds.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.5.1

stunts.name: One With the Water
stunts.text: +2 to defend or overcome with Athletics while swimming.

stunts.name: Ball Toss
stunts.text: Throwing a basketball isn't very different from throwing a knife. You may use your Athletics skill in place of Shoot for thrown weapons.

stunts.name: Equestrian
stunts.text: You can use Athletics instead of Drive whenever you are riding a horse.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.5.3

stunts.name: Graceful Silence
stunts.text: Your natural poise and grace enable you to pass quietly and undetected. You may use your Athletics skill in place of Stealth whenever silence alone would help you move undetected.

stunts.name: Marathon Training
stunts.text: You know how to conserve your energy when undergoing lengthy athletic activity. You may use Athletics instead of Physique during long-distance running, multi-day climbs, and the like.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.5.2

stunts.name: Second-Story Girl
stunts.text: You can use Athletics in place of Burglary for all overcome actions, provided you don’t have to bypass a lock or interact with other security measures.

stunts.name: Whirlwind Step
stunts.text: When you assume the stance of the whirlwind, roll Athletics against Fair (+2) opposition. If you succeed, you may run on vertical surfaces and leap unlikely distances without making rolls to do so, until your next turn ends. If you succeed with style, you may instead gain these benefits for the rest of the scene.

stunts.name: Catch
stunts.text: When defending against an attack with a thrown object, if you succeed with style, you may catch the item that was thrown at you and create a related aspect with a free invoke, instead of just a boost. Details such as your Physique skill and any relevant aspects may be used to determine whether a given object is something you could, practically speaking, catch.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.29.2

stunts.name: Childhood Playground
stunts.text: You are remember the place you grew up in well, and you still find it easy to navigate its obstacles. Name and describe that place. You gain +2 to overcome with Athletics whenever you are in a similar environment.

stunts.name: Flanking Specialist
stunts.text: Once per scene, when you create the aspect Flanked or similar on an opponent, you gain one additional free invocation of the aspect.

stunts.name: Sportsman
stunts.text: Sports are your life. Pick a sport. You get a +2 to all Athletics rolls relating to that sport.

stunts.name: Surefooted
stunts.text: You suffer no increased difficulty to Athletics due to snowdrifts, loose soil, or shifting sand.

stunts.name: The Big Heist
stunts.text: Once per scene, when you case a location you can spend a fate point (and a few minutes of observation) to make a special Burglary roll representing your criminal genius. For each shift you make on this roll you discover or create an aspect on the location, though you may only invoke one of them for free.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.6.2

stunts.name: Mental Blueprint
stunts.text: You’re highly skilled at visualizing the whole of a target based on just a part of it. When casing a location, you receive a +2 on Burglary rolls to create an advantage.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.6.2

stunts.name: Bump and Grab
stunts.text: Your character is exceptionally skilled at taking advantage of distractions in order to make a quick grab. You may spend a fate point to attempt a simple Burglary action – such as picking a pocket, or palming an object – as a free action.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.26.1

stunts.name: Cool Hand
stunts.text: A steady hand can be critical when things get hairy. Your hands never shake and never waver. +2 to overcome actions with Burglary whenever you perform fine manual work.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.26.1

stunts.name: Cutpurse
stunts.text: Once per scene, as a free action, you can attempt to pick the pocket of someone in the same zone as you. Success at no cost on this roll means your victim is not even aware of the theft.

stunts.name: Hatpin Maestro
stunts.text: You don’t ever have to spend a fate point to declare that you have the proper tools for lockpicking or disabling a device, even in extreme situations (like being imprisoned and separated from all your stuff). This source of opposition is just off the table.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.6.2

stunts.name: Preferred Target
stunts.text: Thieves have specialities, just like scientists. Pick a type of location or object (e.g. banks, apartments, handbags). You gain +2 to your Burglary skill when using it against that type of target.

stunts.name: Security Specialist
stunts.text: You don’t have to be present to provide active opposition to someone trying to overcome security measures you put in place or worked on. (Normally, a character would roll against passive opposition for that.)

stunts.name: The Accounting of Small Things
stunts.text: Once you have successfully stolen something small enough to fit in a pocket, it is gone until you choose to reveal it again. No amount of searching—or even stripping—will reveal the purloined item. You may only have one such item at a time hidden in this fashion.

stunts.name: Always a Way Out
stunts.text: +2 on Burglary rolls made to create an advantage whenever you’re trying to escape from a location.

stunts.name: Criminal Mind
stunts.text: +2 on Burglary rolls made to create an advantage when investigating another criminal's work which closely matches a crime you have committed before.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.6.1

stunts.name: Without a Trace
stunts.text: You don’t have to be present to provide active opposition to someone trying to analyse physical evidence that you were present during a crime. (Normally, a character would roll against passive opposition for that.)
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.27.3

stunts.name: Legerdemain
stunts.text: +2 to Burglary rolls made to perform magic tricks.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.26.2

stunts.name: Master of Illusion
stunts.text: The time it takes for you to prepare a large illusion is reduced by two shifts.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.26.2

stunts.name: Stage Magic
stunts.text: You can perform misdirection on a large scale, under appropriately controlled circumstances. Provided you are acting within an arena you control (such as a stage, or an area you have had adequate time to prepare), there are simply no size limitations (within reason) for your Burglary targets.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.26.2

stunts.name: Disable Device
stunts.text: If you can take apart a lock, you can take apart a clock. You may use Burglary instead of Crafts to disassemble anything mechanical.

stunts.name: Five-Fingered Discount
stunts.text: Why buy what you can steal? You may use your Burglary skill instead of your Resources skill to “buy” things. Everything obtained this way has the aspect Stolen Property with one free invocation against you. The difficulty of an attempt to obtain something with Burglary may or may not be the same as the difficulty of an attempt to buy that same thing with Resources, at the GM's discretion. The time required may also vary.

stunts.name: Talk the Talk
stunts.text: You can use Burglary in place of Contacts whenever you’re dealing specifically with other thieves and burglars.

stunts.name: Trespass Tempo
stunts.text: Whenever you’re running a heist, you operate on a very precise internal clock. You may use Burglary instead of Notice to determine turn order as long as everything is going to plan.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.6.1

stunts.name: Tripwire Sensibilities
stunts.text: You’ve run into enough traps that you’ve developed an instinct for avoiding them. You may roll Burglary instead of Investigate or Notice in order to spot or defend against a trap.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.6.1

stunts.name: You’re Never Safe
stunts.text: You can use Burglary to make mental attacks and create advantages against a target, by staging a heist in such a way as to shatter their confidence in their security.

stunts.name: Burglar's Signature
stunts.text: Some element of your character makes you an expert thief. Pick one of your aspects. Once per scene, you may invoke that aspect on a Burglary roll for free.

stunts.name: I, Lupin!
stunts.text: Somehow, you can always pull of a stroke of larcenous brilliance when it really counts. Once per scene, when you succeed on a Burglary roll, you may choose to succeed with style instead.

stunts.name: Center of the Web
stunts.text: Whether or not you lead it, you are like the spider at the center of a web regarding any organization of which you are a part. Information about the organization flows your way naturally, taking one time increment less to reach your attentive ears than it would normally, and so long as you are able to make any sort of contact with the outside world, you are quickly able to find out information about your organization’s dealings. You also gain +1 to Contacts rolls related to your organization.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.18.3

stunts.name: Discreet Enquiries
stunts.text: You are unusually subtle when it comes to gathering information. Whenever you seek information and an opponent rolls Contacts to be alerted to this activity, you may roll active opposition against them.

stunts.name: The Strength of One Becomes the Strength of Many
stunts.text: Once you begin a contacting effort, it becomes self-sustaining, as people you talk to talk to other people, who talk to others in turn. In effect, you will always get an answer; it is only a matter of time.

stunts.name: Ubiquity
stunts.text: First, this stunt steps up the intensity of your Center of the Web stunt – information flows your way a total of two time increments faster. Second, this stunt removes the restriction “so long as you are able to make any sort of contact with the outside world.” Your ties into the organization are so thoroughly widespread that the outside world makes every reasonable effort to stay in contact with you. For a fate point, your organization can even make some fairly unreasonable efforts to stay in contact.

stunts.name: The Bonds of Man Stretch to the Horizon
stunts.text: There is no place where you do not know someone, including places you have never been before. You will find a friend wherever you go.

stunts.name: Bounty Board
stunts.text: Whenever you enter a settlement, you can look for work. After an hour or so, you find a job that either pays well but is dangerous or is not too dangerous but doesn’t pay that well. If you spend a fate point, it both pays well and is not too dangerous.

stunts.name: Criminal Underbelly
stunts.text: Whenever you enter a settlement for the first time, you can spend a fate point to declare that the local criminals know you. Choose one of the following: they have a lead on a promising job, they’ll give you and your companions free room and board for a few weeks, or they’ll help you with something right now but you might owe them afterward.

stunts.name: A Friend in Every Port
stunts.text: Whenever you enter a settlement, you may declare you’ve visited it before and roll Contacts against Fair (+2) opposition. If you succeed, you have a friend there who owes you one favor—nothing costly or life threatening. If you succeed with style, your friend will do any one thing for you that is within his power.

stunts.name: Friends Everywhere
stunts.text: Your network of contacts extends around the world. You never suffer any increased difficulty on Contacts rolls from being in an unfamiliar area.

stunts.name: Absolute Authority
stunts.text: You are good at being in charge. +2 to Contacts as long as you are in a position of direct authority over those you intend to contact.

stunts.name: Chain of Command
stunts.text: You are a soldier, and other soldiers answer to you. Add two to your Contacts skill when using it to deal with soldiers from your organisation.

stunts.name: Common Interests/On the Watch
stunts.text: You know people who know things about the things that you want to know about. Pick a broad subject (e.g. the royal court, baseball, university politics). Add +2 to Contacts when using it to enquire about that subject.

stunts.name: Eye for Talent
stunts.text: +2 to Contacts when seeking promising young people.

stunts.name: I'm Looking for Mr
stunts.text: Brown. You are extremely good at tracking people down. +2 to Contacts whenever you are seeking a specific person whose name you know.

stunts.name: Member
stunts.text: Pick a specific organisation. You belong to that organisation. Whenever you want to get in touch with its other members, gain +2 to Contacts.

stunts.name: Noble Born
stunts.text: +2 to Contacts when seeking another member of the aristocracy.

stunts.name: Renowned Courtesan
stunts.text: +2 to Contacts when seeking lonely people who would be sexually attracted to you.

stunts.name: Salesman's Network
stunts.text: All good salesmen build up a network of satisfied customers over time. Pick a type of product. Add two to your Contacts skill when looking for or dealing with makers, sellers, or notable consumers of that type of product.

stunts.name: Too Cool for School
stunts.text: All the kids wanna be just like you. +2 to Contacts when dealing with young adults of middle school or high school age.

stunts.name: Walk the Walk
stunts.text: Your travels have taken you to every corner of the globe. +2 to Contacts rolls when dealing with foreign lands or cultures.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.7.1

stunts.name: Big Man
stunts.text: Pick a specific field of endeavour, such as crime, business, politics, espionage, or the occult. Within this field, you are considered a person of great importance. You may roll Contacts instead of Resources for anything which might fall under the auspices of members of that field.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.7.2

stunts.name: Big Name
stunts.text: You’re so well known that an awareness of your name has crossed over into other areas as well. The first time you deal with someone who’s heard of you (spending a fate point can assure that they have), and you’re using your name, you get a +2 bonus to a Provoke or Rapport roll.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.7.2

stunts.name: Big Reputation
stunts.text: Your reputation has reached great proportions, and people are willing to believe all sorts of things about you. For a fate point, you may use your Contacts skill instead of Deceive, Rapport, Provoke, or Will, provided those you are dealing with are aware of your reputation (a second fate point will nearly always assure that they are). This stunt combines with the bonus from Big Name, getting the character a +2 to Contacts when using it instead of Provoke or Rapport.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.7.2

stunts.name: Ear to the Ground
stunts.text: Whenever someone initiates a conflict against you in an area where you’ve built a network of contacts, you use Contacts instead of Notice to determine turn order, because you got tipped off in time.

stunts.name: Insider
stunts.text: You are able to navigate bureaucracies easily, not because you understand them, but because you know people embedded in the bureaucracy who can provide shortcuts. You may roll Contacts instead of Resources when dealing with any sort of bureaucratic entanglement.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.7.1

stunts.name: My Buddy Has One of Those
stunts.text: Your friends are very willing to let you borrow whatever you need. You may use your Contacts skill instead of your Resources skill to “buy” things. Everything obtained this way has the aspect Not Actually Mine with one free invocation against you. The difficulty of an attempt to obtain something with Contacts may or may not be the same as the difficulty of an attempt to buy that same thing with Resources, at the GM's discretion. The time required may also vary.

stunts.name: Talk the Talk
stunts.text: Whenever dealing with members of your chosen field, you may roll Contacts instead of Rapport.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.7.2

stunts.name: The Weight of Reputation
stunts.text: You can use Contacts instead of Provoke to create advantages based on the fear generated by the sinister reputation you’ve cultivated for yourself and all the shady associates you have. You should have an appropriate aspect to pair with this stunt.

stunts.name: I Know a Guy Who Knows a Guy
stunts.text: Sometimes it’s not who you know, but who the people you know, know. Many of your contacts are, themselves, very well connected. +2 to Contacts when you attempt to corroborate information you’ve gotten from another of your contacts.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.7.1

stunts.name: Rumormonger
stunts.text: +2 to create an advantage when you plant vicious rumors about someone else.

stunts.name: Always Making Useful Things
stunts.text: You don’t ever have to spend a fate point to declare that you have the proper tools for a particular job using Crafts, even in extreme situations (like being imprisoned and separated from all your stuff). This source of opposition is just off the table.

stunts.name: Big Pocking Wrench
stunts.text: You can do a lot as long as you have your trusty giant wrench on hand. +2 to Crafts when using it to fix or break something with a large wrench, provided the wrench is actually useful for what you are using it for.

stunts.name: Demolitions
stunts.text: You are an expert with explosives. +2 to attack rolls made with Crafts against a target structure whenever you have time to prepare and place charges at its exact weak points.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.12.2

stunts.name: The Tools Are Lesser than the Hand
stunts.text: You can produce master-craftsman-level work with the crudest of tools. With a proper workshop, you can create impossibly amazing devices in the finest da Vinci style.

stunts.name: Workshop of Choice
stunts.text: Pick a specific workshop or machine shop. You know exactly how this place is arranged and how it operates, and gain +2 on Crafts whenever you perform work within it.

stunts.name: Architect of Death
stunts.text: +2 to Crafts rolls when designing, repairing or upgrading weaponry.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.12.2

stunts.name: Favored Material
stunts.text: Choose a type of solid material (e.g. wood, steel, bone). +2 to Crafts when you work predominantly with that substance.

stunts.name: From Another Time
stunts.text: You are intimately familiar with the technology of a time other than the present. Choose a time period other than the present day. Add two to your Crafts skill when working with objects or materials from that time period.

stunts.name: Grease Monkey
stunts.text: If it has an engine and wings, propellers, or wheels, you “get” it, intuitively and completely. +2 to Crafts when dealing with vehicles.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.12.2

stunts.name: Master Bowyer
stunts.text: +2 to Crafts when crafting or repairing bows.

stunts.name: Shipwright
stunts.text: +2 to Crafts when building or repairing boats or ships.

stunts.name: Stonemason
stunts.text: +2 to create advantage with Crafts when assessing or working with stone.

stunts.name: Surgical Strikes
stunts.text: When using Crafts in a conflict involving machinery, you can filter out unwanted targets from whole-zone attacks without having to divide up your shifts (normally, you’d need to divide your roll between your targets).

stunts.name: Taxidermist
stunts.text: +2 to Crafts when preserving, stuffing, or posing dead animals.

stunts.name: Better than New!
stunts.text: Whenever you succeed with style on an overcome action to repair a piece of machinery, you can immediately give it a new situation aspect (with a free invoke) reflecting the improvements you’ve made, instead of just a boost.

stunts.name: Bricoleur
stunts.text: You are skilled at improvising when making or repairing something. +2 to Crafts when you creatively incorporate reused materials into your machine.

stunts.name: Eye For Flaws
stunts.text: +2 to create advantage with Crafts when you examine an object or machine for physical weaknesses.

stunts.name: Hogtie
stunts.text: When you use Crafts to create a Hogtied (or similar) advantage on someone, you can always actively oppose any overcome rolls to escape the hogtie (also using Crafts), even if you’re not there. (Normally, if you weren’t there, the escaping character would roll against passive opposition, making it a lot easier to escape.)

stunts.name: Master Bricoleur
stunts.text: When you succeed on a roll to which the Bricoleur stunt applies, your success takes two time steps less than normal.

stunts.name: Mister Fix-It
stunts.text: You are talented at getting things repaired under time-critical circumstances. The time it takes for you to get something fixed is reduced by two shifts.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.12.2

stunts.name: Scavenger
stunts.text: There is an art to making things quickly out of cannibalized parts. You find it easy, because the people who made the thing you took apart did most of the work. +2 to create advantages with Crafts whenever you disassemble machinery for later re-use.

stunts.name: Skilled Bricoleur
stunts.text: Necessity is the mother of invention. +2 to Crafts when you have nothing to build with except inappropriate materials.

stunts.name: Thump of Restoration/Percussive Maintenance
stunts.text: Sometimes a bunch of repairs can get short-handed with a good swift thump. To activate this ability, spend a fate point and roll Crafts (vs. a target of Mediocre). If your roll succeeds, the device or contraption starts working and continues working for a number of exchanges equal to the shifts gained on the Crafts roll. Once the time is up, the device stops working again, and any efforts to repair it are at a one step higher difficulty (since, after all, you hit the thing). If you wish to thump again, you may do so for another fate point, but the difficulty for the Crafts roll increases by one on each subsequent attempt.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.12.2

stunts.name: Locksmith
stunts.text: If you can take apart a clock, you can take apart a lock. You may roll Crafts instead of Burglary when lockpicking.

stunts.name: Personalized Weaponry Engineering
stunts.text: Clever engineering can compensate for a lack of combat skill. Pick a broad category of weapon (e.g. swords, polearms, crossbows). When you wield a weapon of this sort that you have created yourself, you may attack with Crafts instead of Fight (for melee weapons) or Shoot (for ranged weapons). Such weapons will often include odd devices and unusual features that make their use very different from that of a normal weapon.

stunts.name: Brilliant Disguise
stunts.text: Once per scene, when you succeed on a Deceive roll to create a disguise, you succeed with style instead.

stunts.name: Cover
stunts.text: You have a cover identity you can assume. Describe your cover identity, choose a high concept and a trouble aspect for your cover identity, and choose an apex skill for your cover identity. You can assume that identity with enough preparation and the expenditure of a fate point. While you’re in that identity, its high concept and trouble replace yours and you can use Deceive in place of its apex skill. You lose these benefits as soon as your cover is blown, and you may have to spend some time creating a new cover identity.

stunts.name: Double Life
stunts.text: If you are in disguise at the start of a scene, you gain the aspect Definitely Not <your real name> with one free invocation. If you are not in disguise at the start of a scene, you gain the aspect Definitely Not <your secret identity> with one free invocation. These aspects go away at the end of each scene.

stunts.name: Infiltrator
stunts.text: While you are Disguised as Someone Insignificant (see Master of Disguise) you may make a single Investigate roll against a target of Mediocre. Each shift gained can be used to do one of two things: gain a useful (but general) piece of information about the area or group being infiltrated, or leave a clue, hint or message for another character without revealing yourself.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.8.2

stunts.name: Instant Cover
stunts.text: You can whip up a cover story like no one’s business, even if you haven’t made an effort to establish it beforehand. Any time you overcome an obstacle in public using Deceive, automatically add a situation aspect representing your cover story, and stick a free invocation on it.

stunts.name: Master of Disguise
stunts.text: You can convincingly pass yourself off as nearly anyone with a little time and preparation. To use this ability, you pay a fate point to disappear from the scene, gaining the Disguised as Someone Insignificant aspect on yourself. At any subsequent point during play, you choose any nameless NPC in a scene and reveal that that character is actually you in disguise! You may remain in this state for as long as you choose, but if anyone is tipped off that you might be nearby, they may spend a fate point and roll Investigate against your Deceive to overcome the aspect. If the investigator wins, he gets to decide which filler character is actually you in disguise (“Wait a minute – you’re the Emerald Emancipator!”).
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.8.2

stunts.name: Mimicry
stunts.text: You may create advantages with Deceive related to imitating the mannerisms and voice of anyone you’ve had a chance to study. Studying someone usually requires only an investment of time, and not a roll of the dice – at least half an hour of constant exposure. This timeframe can be reduced, but will require an Empathy, Investigate, or Deceive roll against a target of Mediocre - any shifts you get on the roll reduce the time required.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.8.2

stunts.name: One Person, Many Faces
stunts.text: Whenever you meet someone new, you can spend a fate point to declare that you’ve met that person before, but under a different name and identity. Create a situation aspect to represent your cover story, and you can use Deceive in place of Rapport whenever interacting with that person.

stunts.name: Perfect Reflection
stunts.text: +2 to create advantage or defend with Deceive when you are disguised as someone you know well and that disguise is in question.

stunts.name: Quick Disguise
stunts.text: You’re able to put together a convincing disguise in a heartbeat, using items from your surroundings. You can roll Deceive to create a disguise without any time to prepare, in nearly any situation.

stunts.name: Trick the Toffs
stunts.text: +2 to Deceive when you disguise yourself as someone from the upper classes.

stunts.name: Versatile Disguises
stunts.text: You suffer no increased difficulty on Deceive rolls when disguising yourself as a person of different gender, height, skin tone, or age.

stunts.name: Dead For Sure
stunts.text: While you are Feigning Death, no-one will even check to see if you really are dead until all of your allies have conceded or been taken out.

stunts.name: Fast Feint
stunts.text: Once per scene, you may roll Deceive to perform a feint as a free action.

stunts.name: Feint
stunts.text: When it looks like you're going to go right, you go left. And vice versa. +2 to create advantages with Deceive that relate to confusion and misdirection in physical combat.

stunts.name: Feint En Masse
stunts.text: You may feint against every opponent in your zone in one action, dividing your shifts between them.

stunts.name: Impenetrable Bluff
stunts.text: You can bluff like a poker pro. Maybe you are a poker pro. +2 to create advantages or defend with Deceive when using it to trick people into believing that you are more capable or better positioned than you actually are.

stunts.name: Not a Threat
stunts.text: Choose Deceive or Stealth when you take this stunt. When you create an advantage with that skill to make yourself as non-threatening or unobtrusive as possible, enemies will find other targets for as long as that aspect exists. As soon as you successfully attack someone, the aspect goes away.

stunts.name: Play Dead
stunts.text: When you place an aspect like Feigning Death on yourself, no-one can attack you while the aspect remains in play.

stunts.name: Superior Feint
stunts.text: Whenever you place an aspect on an opponent using the Feint stunt, you may defend against their melee attacks with Deceive until that aspect goes away.

stunts.name: Worthy Cringe
stunts.text: +2 to create advantage with Deceive when you try to appear unthreatening during a physical combat.

stunts.name: Crooked Dealer in Antiquities
stunts.text: +2 to create advantages with Deceive based on the (false) monetary value of archaeological finds.

stunts.name: Crooked Salesman
stunts.text: You are skilled at subtly misrepresenting your goods or services to customers. +2 to Deceive when using it to sell something.

stunts.name: Faustian Pact
stunts.text: Your job is to trick people into signing unfair contracts. When you have a copy of such a contract to hand, you gain +2 on Deceive rolls to fool people into thinking it is fair.

stunts.name: Grifter/Professional Panhandler
stunts.text: You profit from your lies, literally. +2 to Deceive when using it to fool someone into giving you money.

stunts.name: The Devil's Own Luck
stunts.text: On games of pure chance, like roulette, where a character could not normally roll a skill to affect the outcome, you may use your Deceive skill at its full value.
stunts.requires: one other stunt relating to gambling
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.14.1

stunts.name: Double or Nothing
stunts.text: Once per scene, when involved in a game of chance, you can declare "Double or Nothing!" This is a call for both sides to reroll (and as such doesn’t involve fate points). If you win the next roll, the initial exchange is treated as a scratch (no loss to any participants), but if you lose (by whatever amount) the number of shifts you lose by is doubled. Regardless of the result, such a move often elevates the stakes of a game. This can turn a regular stakes game into a high stakes one, and a high stakes game into a matter of life and death.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.14.1

stunts.name: Know When to Fold 'Em
stunts.text: Whenever gambling with NPCs, you may ask that the GM roll the NPC’s Deceit in advance. Whenever the GM does this, the roll is automatically considered to be secret – she doesn’t have to show it to anyone. The twist is that the GM must indicate to you whether the NPC’s roll is above or below your Deceive skill – just not by how much. Given this knowledge, you may then choose whether you participates, or excuses yourself, from the gambling contest. If you do participate, the GM reveals the value of the roll, and may still spend fate points on behalf of her NPC as usual once the contest starts in earnest.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.14.2

stunts.name: Winnings
stunts.text: You win at the gambling tables more than you lose, and are often flush with cash. Once per session, you may use Deceive instead of Resources to represent these winnings, so long as you haven’t recently experienced a loss. You must provide a quick one-sentence explanation of what the resource is and how you won it, when using this stunt.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.14.2

stunts.name: Corroboration of Coincidence
stunts.text: Fate favors your lies with minor coincidences and circumstantial evidence that seem to lend them credence. You may apply a boost to the scene before you roll Deceive, so long as you can describe how it helps you look more honest. If successful, the boost turns into an aspect on the scene.

stunts.name: Hey, What’s That?
stunts.text: Gain a +2 bonus whenever you’re using Deceive to momentarily distract someone, as long as part of the distraction involves saying something.

stunts.name: Houdini
stunts.text: You could be found by the police standing next to a burned-down church with a handful of matches and a can of gasoline and still get away scot-free. +2 to Deceive when using it to defend against attempts to discern or prove your involvement in a crime.

stunts.name: Low Profile
stunts.text: You always provide active opposition to attempts to locate you with Investigate.

stunts.name: The Appearance of Wealth
stunts.text: You seem like a wealthy and powerful person, regardless of the reality. You may use Deceive in place of Resources as long as no actual money or goods need to change hands.

stunts.name: Con Man
stunts.text: You are a bona fide confidence man, and that lets you get a read on people, easy. You may use Deceive instead of Empathy to read a person’s emotional state and get a general sense of who they are, but the type of aspects that may be assessed or created are limited to things like their trouble or other negatively skewed/easily exploitable aspects.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.8.1

stunts.name: "Honest" Lawyer
stunts.text: Okay, maybe they don’t exist. But most people would say that you are one, anyway. You may use Deceit instead of Lore whenever knowledge of the law or legal matters are involved.

stunts.name: Illusion of Grandeur
stunts.text: Making a good first impression is all about misrepresenting yourself. Whenever you meet a new person, you may use Deceit instead of Rapport to influence them. This option vanishes as soon as you fail one of the Deceit rolls.

stunts.name: It's Just Creative Lying
stunts.text: Really, acting is just an advanced form of lying. You may use your Deceive skill instead of Rapport when acting.

stunts.name: Mind Games
stunts.text: You can use Deceive in place of Provoke to make mental attacks, as long as you can make up a clever lie as part of the attack.

stunts.name: Players' Club
stunts.text: You’ve played in so many games, and in so many places, that it’s rare that you can’t find someone who knows you. You may use your Deceit skill instead of Contacts whenever making a Contacts roll – though doing so invariably colors the results with the nature of gambling.
stunts.requires: one other stunt relating to gambling
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.14.2

stunts.name: Shield of Lies
stunts.text: Your lies run so deep that you almost believe them yourself. You may use Deceive to defend against mental attacks whenever an opponent focuses on a truth you consistently deny.

stunts.name: Takes One to Know One
stunts.text: As an accomplished liar, you’re especially able to figure out when someone else is lying as well. You may use Deceive instead of Empathy to defend against Deceive actions.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.8.3

stunts.name: Bait of Words
stunts.text: Gain an additional +2 to Deceive whenever you invoke an advantage you personally created by speaking to the target and rolling Rapport.

stunts.name: Fast Talk
stunts.text: You get a +2 to overcome obstacles with Deceive, provided you don’t have to talk to the person you’re trying to deceive for more than a few sentences before blowing past them.

stunts.name: Founded Upon Lies
stunts.text: You are very good at turning innocuous lies into devastating ones. Once per scene, when you succeed on a Deceit roll, you may succeed with style instead.

stunts.name: The Honest Lie
stunts.text: The best lies are the ones that contain a healthy dose of truth. You gain a +2 to Deceive whenever you incorporate a hefty portion of the truth into a lie. The truth must be relevant, not unimportant, and significant, not trivial – it must be on par with (or bigger than) the lie, or at least in the ballpark.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.8.3

stunts.name: Lies upon Lies
stunts.text: +2 to create a Deceive advantage against someone who has believed one of your lies already during this session.

stunts.name: Master Manipulator
stunts.text: You can treat other people like chess pieces and make it work. +2 to attack and create advantages with Deceive whenever you try to trick your target into following a preset plan of yours.

stunts.name: One Big Lie
stunts.text: Pick one specific statement that isn't true. You gain +2 to Deceive when using it to convince someone that that statement is true.

stunts.name: City Driver
stunts.text: You've spent most of your life driving up and down the same streets. Pick a city. Whenever you are in that city, you never suffer increased difficulty on Drive rolls due to traffic.

stunts.name: Defensive Driving
stunts.text: You’re good at keeping your car in one piece. +2 to overcome with Drive during a chase.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.9.2

stunts.name: Barnstormer
stunts.text: You can squeeze your plane through places where it has no business fitting. You never need to spend a fate point to declare details relating to your plane having enough clearance space to fly or land. What’s more, if you do spend a fate point, you can fit the plane in places you absolutely should not be able to.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.21.1

stunts.name: Death from Above
stunts.text: While in flight, if you are able to make an attack on another flying target from an elevated position, you do two additional points of stress on a successful hit. However, this action takes you out of your position of advantage.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.21.1

stunts.name: Fly By Night
stunts.text: Whether in dead of night or during a storm, your piloting skills remain true. You never face increased difficulties due to environmental factors (darkness, weather) when flying. This does not protect your plane from taking damage from the environment – but your skill remains unreduced.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.21.1

stunts.name: Walk Away From It
stunts.text: You have a great instinct for crash-landing planes, and are able to walk away from even the most catastrophic-seeming landings. While you are piloting a plane into its crash landing, coincidence conspires to keep you and your passengers alive, and you pass from the view of the other combatants. You may re-enter play in any subsequent scene in as dramatic a fashion as you see fit, explaining to everyone how you survived. You return with all of your physical stress cleared and a single additional consequence incurred to reflect the dangers you defied.
stunts.requires: at least two other Drive stunts
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.21.1

stunts.name: Bareback Rider
stunts.text: You suffer no increasing difficulty to Drive rolls while riding an animal due to a lack of saddle, reins, or other tack.

stunts.name: Breaking It In
stunts.text: You’re skilled at breaking in new mounts. You receive +2 on all Drive rolls during such an effort. (We suggest you run breaking in a mount as a conflict between rider and steed. The rider should make mental attacks using Drive vs. Will on the animal while the animal is making Athletics or Physique vs. Drive physical attacks on the rider. When one party is finally taken out, takes a consequence, or concedes, either the animal is broken or the rider is thrown.)
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.28.3

stunts.name: Hell Bent for Leather
stunts.text: You know how to get the best speed out of your mount. +2 to Drive whenever you're on horseback and riding at top speed. You must be an active participant in driving your mount forward in order to receive this bonus. The benefit doesn’t apply if you’re, say, in the saddle, but unconscious.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.28.3

stunts.name: Mounted Trample
stunts.text: Once per scene, when you succeed with style on a create advantage roll with Drive and place an aspect on an opponent, you may exchange one of your free invocations for a 2-shift hit on that opponent.

stunts.name: Preferred Mount
stunts.text: Choose a type of riding animal. +2 to overcome or create advantage with Drive when mounted on that kind of animal.

stunts.name: Ride Anything
stunts.text: If it can be ridden like a riding beast, you can ride it. You suffer no increased difficulty for a lack of familiarity, no matter how strange the mount.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.28.3

stunts.name: Run Them Down
stunts.text: +2 to attack with Drive when you try to trample someone with your horse.

stunts.name: We Ride as One
stunts.text: You fight and act on horseback without penalty, and nothing can knock you off. Any time you would take a physical consequence, you can opt for the horse to take it instead — the horse having a similar consequence track to your character.

stunts.name: Sailor
stunts.text: +2 to Drive whenever you use it to operate a water-borne vessel.

stunts.name: Flying Ace
stunts.text: You are a skilled combat pilot, and as such may roll Drive instead of Shoot to attack in a dogfight.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.21.1

stunts.name: Gunner
stunts.text: You’re a former military man with the training to use vehicle-mounted weaponry. You may use your Drive skill to make attacks with such weapons.

stunts.name: Mechanic
stunts.text: You may roll Drive instead of Crafts when working on a wheeled vehicle.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.9.1

stunts.name: Mounted Combat
stunts.text: You may roll Drive instead of Fight to make melee attacks whenever you are riding an animal.

stunts.name: Old Salt
stunts.text: You may use Drive instead of Lore to make predictions about the weather.

stunts.name: Plane Mechanic
stunts.text: You may roll Drive instead of Crafts when working on a vehicle capable of flight.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.21.2

stunts.name: Traffic Watcher
stunts.text: You really know how to use those rear-view mirrors. You may use Drive instead of Notice to be aware of vehicles and road conditions, to detect vehicular ambushes, and to determine turn order while operating a vehicle.

stunts.name: Flawless Navigation
stunts.text: The skies (or roads) are an open map in your mind. +2 to Drive when navigating to a strange place or overcoming being Lost.

stunts.name: Hard to Shake
stunts.text: +2 to Drive whenever you’re pursuing another vehicle in a chase scene.

stunts.name: One Hand on the Wheel
stunts.text: Multitasking behind the wheel is second nature to you. +2 to overcome with Drive after you successfully create an advantage in a contest.

stunts.name: Pedal to the Metal
stunts.text: You can coax more speed out of your vehicle than seems possible. Whenever you’re engaged in any contest where speed is the primary factor (such as a chase or race of some kind) and you tie with your Drive roll, it’s considered a success.

stunts.name: Ramming Speed!
stunts.text: When ramming another vehicle, you ignore two shifts of damage. So if you ram and hit for four shifts, you only take two yourself.

stunts.name: Signature Ride
stunts.text: You’ve used a certain vehicle so much that its operation is instinctive to you. Pick a specific make and model of vehicle. Add two to your Drive skill when using that sort of vehicle.

stunts.name: Steady Driver
stunts.text: Once per scene, you may reroll a failed Drive roll for free.

stunts.name: Turn on a Dime
stunts.text: Somehow, no matter how crazy you drive, you always seem to pull it off. +2 to Drive when making very tight turns and trying to fit through very narrow spaces.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.9.2

stunts.name: Unsafe at Any Speed
stunts.text: You are the bane of curbside markets and rickety struts holding up awnings. When you hit an object other than a character or vehicle, increase the stress you cause by 2. Any time an object is taken out by the damage, the result should be spectacular – an explosion or collapse.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.9.2

stunts.name: Architecture of the Heart
stunts.text: Reading a room is a triviality to you. Even more, you can spot the emotional lynchpins in a room and easily understand how actions would impact the mood. If you roll Empathy to read a room—difficulty Mediocre (+0)—count how many shifts you accrue. Over the course of the scene, you may ask the GM to tell you how people would react to any hypothetical scenario. You can do this a number of times equal to the number of shifts generated.

stunts.name: The Artist's Eye
stunts.text: When you encounter a work of art, you may use Empathy to read the artist's emotional state, as if you had had interpersonal contact with them. You may also create advantages with Empathy related to the authenticity of the work.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.4.1

stunts.name: Cold Read
stunts.text: Once per scene, you may use Empathy to read a person's emotional state without the need for interpersonal contact.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.10.2

stunts.name: Heart's Secret
stunts.text: When you successfully use Empathy to read a person's emotional state, if that person's aspects are secret, the aspects the GM reveals must be those that are of the utmost importance to the person, unless you explicitly instruct her otherwise. If the person's aspects are not secret, you may choose which one to attach each of your free invocations to.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century, §6.10.2

stunts.name: A Peek Inside
stunts.text: You achieve such a strong understanding of your subject that you can start to make some fairly accurate guesses about his behavior. After you have successfully read a person's emotional state, you may immediately ask the GM a hypothetical question about that person’s motives, which the GM must be able to answer with "yes", "no", or "maybe", to the best of her ability. The question must speak to the kind of person the target is, not things they’ve done, though it may ask if they are capable of doing such things. If the GM answers with a "maybe", you may ask a second question to get clarification. This second question may seek details, rather than another one-word answer.
stunts.requires: at least two other Empathy stunts
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century, §6.10.2

stunts.name: Read You Like a Book
stunts.text: People's emotions are pretty damn obvious to you. +2 to create advantages with Empathy when using it to read a person's emotional state.

stunts.name: The Truth of Who You Are
stunts.text: Every two minutes of conversation you have with someone reveals one of their aspects. However, for every two aspects you learn, you reveal one of your own to that person and anyone listening. Round down, so the first one you learn is free.

stunts.name: You've Got Issues
stunts.text: +2 to create advantage with Empathy on a character's trouble aspect.

stunts.name: I’ve Heard Every Lie in the Book
stunts.text: +2 to overcome or defend against lies with Empathy.

stunts.name: The Inner Eye Sees Inner Truth
stunts.text: Without rolling, you can tell if another character is lying so long as the target’s Deceive is equal to or lower than your Empathy. In the case of high Deceive, you will know that you cannot tell, but will never receive a “false positive.”

stunts.name: Lie Whisperer
stunts.text: +2 to all Empathy rolls made to discern or discover lies, whether they’re directed at you or someone else.

stunts.name: Truth Beyond the Lie
stunts.text: Once per scene, when you successfully see through a lie, you may gain a free invocation on whichever of the liar’s aspects is most closely associated with their reason for lying to you.

stunts.name: Animal Empathy
stunts.text: You can use Empathy in place of Lore to sense the emotions of animals.

stunts.name: Hit Them Where It Hurts/Disturbingly Insightful
stunts.text: Your skill at reading people makes you adept at provoking a strong emotional response if you’re trying to get them angry, depressed, or something similar. You may use Empathy in place of Provoke to make mental attacks.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century, §6.10.2

stunts.name: Nose for Trouble
stunts.text: You can use Empathy instead of Notice to determine your turn order in a physical conflict, provided you’ve gotten a chance to observe or speak to those involved for at least a few minutes beforehand during this scene.

stunts.name: One Breath
stunts.text: A true samurai can size up a foe within a single breath. You may use Empathy to read when a person will attack you and evaluate their combat skills.

stunts.name: Track the Soul
stunts.text: Your understanding of people you’ve met is sufficiently strong that it gives you an easy sense of how to find them. You may roll Empathy instead of Investigate whenever you’re tracking down or otherwise trying to find someone you’ve met before.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.10.1

stunts.name: Bartender's Ear
stunts.text: Like any good bartender, you know how to understand drunk people. Add two to your Empathy skill when dealing with people who are under the influence of alcohol.

stunts.name: Ebb and Flow
stunts.text: You are so aware of the social currents in a situation that you are able to see something of what’s coming before it arrives. At the beginning of any exchange, you may spend a fate point to attempt to create an advantage with Empathy. You may then act normally on your turn as usual.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.10.1

stunts.name: Listening Ear
stunts.text: +2 to overcome or create advantage with Empathy when you listen to another person for half an hour or more.

stunts.name: Preemptive Grace
stunts.text: You are so tuned into social situations that you may act quickly and decisively to shape the situation to your liking. +2 to Empathy for the purposes of determining turn order in a conflict.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.10.1

stunts.name: Psychologist
stunts.text: Once per session you can reduce someone else’s consequence by one level of severity (severe to moderate, moderate to mild, mild to nothing at all) by succeeding on an Empathy roll with a difficulty of Fair (+2) for a mild consequence, Good (+3) for moderate, or Great (+4) for severe. You need to talk with the person you’re treating for at least half an hour in order for them to receive the benefits of this stunt, and you can’t use it on yourself. (Normally, this roll would only start the recovery process, instead of changing the consequence level.)

stunts.name: Army of One/The King Still Stands
stunts.text: You are a one-man army; the odds don’t matter to you. Whenever you are physically attacked by a mob, opponents in that mob do not get a teamwork bonus to their attacks.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.13.1

stunts.name: Army on the Edge of My Blade
stunts.text: You take no penalty—and grant no bonus—for being outnumbered, no matter how preposterous the numbers.

stunts.name: Brawler
stunts.text: You’re at home in any big old burly brawl, with multiple opponents and ideally some beer in you. When fighting a mob of nameless NPCs, you deal one additional stress on a successful physical hit.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.13.1

stunts.name: Follow-Through
stunts.text: Once per conflict, when you inflict a physical consequence on an opponent with Fight, you may also inflict a 2-point physical hit on another opponent in the same zone.

stunts.name: Whirlwind Attack
stunts.text: You may make a Fight attack against every opponent in your zone, dividing your roll between them as you see fit.

stunts.name: Advanced Warmaster
stunts.text: When you’re fighting anyone who is armed with a sword, you get a further +2 bonus to creating an advantage using Warmaster.

stunts.name: Destroyer of Abominations
stunts.text: You hit harder when your enemy is something blasphemous. You gain +2 to attacks with Fight against creatures that are unusually offensive to your faith.

stunts.name: Favored Enemy
stunts.text: Choose an organisation or ethnic group. You gain +2 on attacks made with Fight against a member of that group. (Exercise discretion in the use of this stunt. A racist villain is probably OK, but a racist PC is almost certainly not.)

stunts.name: Favored Enemy Parry
stunts.text: Choose an organisation. You gain +2 to defend with Fight against members of that group.

stunts.name: Mirror Stance
stunts.text: Your unusual fighting style lets you defend effortlessly when you and your opponent are similarly armed. +2 to defend with Fight whenever your opponent attacks you with the same kind of weapon as you wield.

stunts.name: Reflection Shatters the Mirror
stunts.text: You can switch in a heartbeat from matching your opponent move for move to doing precisely the opposite. +2 to attack with Fight whenever your opponent wields the same kind of weapon as you do. (adapted from http://dfrpg-* Unorthodox Fighting. People with formal training are less able to defend against your tomfoolery in combat. +2 to attacks with Fight against opponents who strictly adhere to a formal style of combat.

stunts.name: Riposte
stunts.text: If you succeed with style on a Fight defense, you can choose to inflict a 2-shift hit rather than take a boost.

stunts.name: Turnabout
stunts.text: When you succeed with style on a Fight defense, instead of taking a boost, you may spend a fate point to inflict physical stress equal to the shifts you got on your defense roll. You may only do this once per opponent per scene.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.29.1

stunts.name: Ally’s Shield
stunts.text: You can invoke Dwarven Shield-Maiden when a nearby ally suffers an attack. When you do, redirect that attack to yourself. Your defense is Average (+1) against that attack.

stunts.name: Defend the Weak
stunts.text: When someone is attacked physically while within your zone, you can spend a fate point to redirect that attack to yourself. You may defend against that attack at +1.

stunts.name: Leave My Friends Alone!
stunts.text: +2 to attack with Fight when your opponent’s most recent action was to attack one of your allies.

stunts.name: Close at Hand
stunts.text: You can bring your weapon to hand faster than the eye can track. If the difficulty of overcoming an aspect of Disarmed or similar is Fair (+2) or less, you may overcome it as a free action. If the difficulty is higher, instead gain +2 on the roll to overcome that aspect.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.15.3

stunts.name: Disarming Specialist
stunts.text: You have been trained in how to disarm an armed combatant. Once per scene per opponent, when you successfully defend against an attack with a melee weapon, you may sacrifice your next action to place the Disarmed aspect on that opponent.

stunts.name: Firm Grip
stunts.text: +2 to defend with Fight against being disarmed.

stunts.name: Fists of Fury
stunts.text: Swinging wildly and with force, you can strike at an opponent over and over again, wearing down his defense with each blow. +2 to Fight whenever you punch an opponent who is using full defense.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.13.1

stunts.name: Flawless Parry/Perfect Parry
stunts.text: +2 to defend with Fight when you perform a full defense action.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.29.1

stunts.name: Guard Breaker
stunts.text: When you attack someone who is performing a full defense action, you gain +2 to Fight.

stunts.name: Blind-Fight
stunts.text: Your ability to attack with Fight works unimpeded by conditions like darkness or other visual impairments.

stunts.name: Master of the Roof
stunts.text: +2 to defend with Fight when you are at a higher elevation than your opponent.

stunts.name: Mountain Warrior
stunts.text: +2 to defend with Fight when your opponent is at a higher elevation than you.

stunts.name: Precise Swing
stunts.text: You suffer no increased difficulty on Fight rolls from aspects related to cover.

stunts.name: Tunnel Fighter
stunts.text: Your Fight skill works unimpeded by conditions such as narrow passages, low ceilings, or other spatial limitations.

stunts.name: Ride-By Attack
stunts.text: Once per scene, you may move one zone while mounted, attack with Fight, and then move one additional zone, provided there are no situation aspects restricting movement.

stunts.name: Unhorse
stunts.text: +2 to create advantage with Fight when you try to remove someone from their mount’s back.

stunts.name: Bull Charge
stunts.text: You know how to use your momentum in a fight. +2 to attack with Fight whenever you move at least one zone unopposed before you attack with a fist or other blunt weapon.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.13.2

stunts.name: Dispatch the Fallen
stunts.text: Once per scene, when you attack an enemy who is Prone, Knocked to the Ground, or similar, you gain +2 to attack with Fight.

stunts.name: Flying Kick
stunts.text: You are able to leap through the air, leading with a powerful kick that can lay an unsuspecting opponent out. +2 to attack with Fight whenever you move at least one zone unopposed before you attack with a kick.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.13.2

stunts.name: Killing Stroke
stunts.text: Once per scene, when you force an opponent to take a consequence, you can spend a fate point to increase the consequence’s severity (so mild becomes moderate, moderate becomes severe). If your opponent was already going to take a severe consequence, he must either take a severe consequence and a second consequence or be taken out.

stunts.name: Knockback
stunts.text: When you succeed with style on an attack with Fight, you may choose to reduce the value of your hit by one in order to move your opponent one zone, provided there are no situation aspects impeding this movement.

stunts.name: Signature Strike
stunts.text: You have a specific attack which you have honed to devastating perfection. Describe it as an aspect (for instance Thousand Whirlwinds Strike As One! or Kick in the Crotch). Once per conflict, as a free action, you can attach this aspect to an opponent as a boost.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.13.1

stunts.name: Spring Attack
stunts.text: Once per scene, you may move one zone on foot, attack with Fight, and then move one additional zone, provided there are no situation aspects restricting movement.

stunts.name: Stunning Fist
stunts.text: Once per physical conflict, when you succeed on an unarmed attack, you may place the aspect Stunned on your opponent with one free invocation.

stunts.name: Do You Like It?
stunts.text: I Made It Myself. A weapon you made yourself is a weapon that you know really well. +2 to defend with Fight when opponents attempt to disarm you or turn the limitations of your weapon against you.

stunts.name: My Blade Strikes True
stunts.text: Once per conflict, you can force the opponent to use a mild consequence instead of a 2-point stress box on a successful Fight attack with your heirloom sword.

stunts.name: Two Sword Joe
stunts.text: Normally, fighting with two swords just looks cool, but when you wield two swords, you have a decisive advantage. Any time you succeed on an attack with two swords, the stress inflicted is increased by one.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.15.4

stunts.name: Anything Goes
stunts.text: Virtually anything can be a lethal weapon in your hands, as long as you can comfortably and casually lift it. You never need to spend a fate point in order to declare that an improvised weapon is close at hand, unless your surroundings have been deliberately prepared against this (such as a prison cell).
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.29.3

stunts.name: Weapons of the World
stunts.text: Every kind of proper (not improvised) hand-held melee weapon in the world has been in your hands at one point or another. Once per conflict, when you handle an unusual weapon of this type, you may tell a quick two- or three-sentence story (either to another character or as an internal monologue) to gain a +2 on your next roll with it.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.29.3

stunts.name: Bloodlust
stunts.text: Once per scene, when you inflict a physical consequence, you gain one additional invocation of that consequence.

stunts.name: Demoralising Stance/My Weapon Speaks For Me/Talking With My Fists
stunts.text: As a trained fighter, you are able to adopt a stance that makes it unequivocally clear how capable you are of handing someone his ass. Whenever displaying your fighting stance or threatening someone with violence, you may roll Fight instead of Provoke to scare them.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.13.2

stunts.name: Hidden Weapons
stunts.text: Your knowledge of weapons helps you conceal them. You may use Fight instead of Burglary to conceal weaponry.

stunts.name: Mixed Martial Artist
stunts.text: You practice judo or another grappling-based martial art. You may use Fight instead of Physique to create advantages related to wrestling and pinning.

stunts.name: Parry Everything
stunts.text: Your hand-eye coordination is superb, and perhaps you could even deflect a bullet with your weapon. You may use Fight to defend against Shoot attacks. (The GM may limit this stunt by having it only apply to slower projectiles or those fired from another zone.)

stunts.name: Whip Grip
stunts.text: You can use Fight to grab things with a whip.

stunts.name: Armiger
stunts.text: Whenever you take a mild physical consequence, you can choose to instead destroy your armor or your shield, provided you’re using the appropriate item. Once your armor or shield is destroyed, you’ll have to get it repaired or get a new one.

stunts.name: Backup Weapon
stunts.text: Whenever someone’s about to hit you with a Disarmed situation aspect or something similar, spend a fate point to declare you have a backup weapon. Instead of a situation aspect, your opponent gets a boost, representing the momentary distraction you suffer having to switch.

stunts.name: Dirty Fighter
stunts.text: You have a talent for fighting dirty and are experienced in pulling all manner of tricks in order to get the upper hand on your opponents. Any time you invoke an opponent’s aspect in a physical fight, you get an additional +1 on the roll.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.13.1

stunts.name: Competition Fighting
stunts.text: You excel on the mat or in the ring. +2 to attack with Fight as long as the combat is part of an adjudicated sport and is not a matter of life and death.

stunts.name: Cut Off
stunts.text: When someone defends against your Fight roll, and they succeed with style, they do not receive a boost.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.3.1

stunts.name: The Drunkard Swings Wide
stunts.text: Your blows are crude and telegraphed, but in dodging, your opponent seems to be struck by an elbow or a knee by accident. Make your Fight roll as normal. If you strike your opponent, you do stress as normal. If you miss or tie, your opponent takes one physical stress anyway.

stunts.name: Ground and Pound
stunts.text: When you successfully attack someone with Fight whom you are grappling, you inflict 2 additional stress.

stunts.name: Heavy Hitter
stunts.text: When you succeed with style on a Fight attack and choose to reduce the result by one to gain a boost, you gain a full situation aspect with a free invocation instead.

stunts.name: Hold the Line
stunts.text: When you share a zone with an ally who also has this stunt, you gain +2 to defend with Fight.

stunts.name: Kick the Bruise
stunts.text: It really hurts to take two hits to the same place. Once per conflict, when you invoke a physical consequence on a successful Fight attack, you can spend a fate point to increase that consequence's severity (so mild becomes moderate, moderate becomes severe) before your opponent takes stress from your successful attack. If you invoked a severe consequence, your opponent must either take a consequence from your attack or be taken out.

stunts.name: Martial Arts
stunts.text: You have an acute insight into the means and methods of barehanded warfare. +2 to create advantages with Fight when you assess another martial artist's style.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.13.2

stunts.name: Brickbreaker/Board Breaking
stunts.text: You are able to focus the force of your blows into a concentrated, small area that is devastating to solid materials. You may make attacks with your body against objects that would typically only be damaged by weapons or tools. If you attack something softer, such as wood, any stress you deal is doubled.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.13.2

stunts.name: Fist of Death
stunts.text: By concentrating your force into a powerful blow, you may devastate even the most potent of opponents. Once per opponent per fight, you may spend a fate point after landing a successful blow to cause your opponent to check their highest unchecked physical stress box (instead of taking stress equal to the shifts you succeeded by).
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.13.2

stunts.name: Martial Scholar
stunts.text: Once you know your opponent, besting them is easy. When you successfully create an advantage with Fight based on assessing an opponent's combat style, you gain an extra free invocation.

stunts.name: Right Back At You
stunts.text: Once per scene, when you succeed with style on a Fight defence against a Shoot attack, you may send the projectile flying back towards your attacker, inflicting a 2-shift physical hit on them.

stunts.name: Spears of Green Wood
stunts.text: You may train a body of troops—unnamed characters in a group of up to approximately 100—for a week and increase their Fight Skill by +1. You can repeat this multiple times, improving any given unit to a maximum of your Fight -2.

stunts.name: Steady the Drunkard
stunts.text: You stagger and seem about to fall, so you reach out and grab your opponent’s arm to steady yourself. This seemingly unintentional grip blocks chi and paralyzes your opponent. You may place a Chi Blocked situation aspect with a free invocation on your opponent. Your opponent may not use any kung fu stunts until they remove this aspect.

stunts.name: Use Their Strength Against Them
stunts.text: Excessive strength can be a disadvantage if your opponent knows how to exploit it. +2 to Fight rolls made to defend against an opponent, provided the opponent is physically much stronger than you.

stunts.name: Warmaster
stunts.text: +2 to Fight rolls made to create an advantage against an opponent, provided the opponent has a fighting style or weakness you can exploit.

stunts.name: Weapon Finesse
stunts.text: +2 to create advantages with Fight related to fancy but harmless bladework, such as cutting your insignia into your opponent’s clothing.

stunts.name: Eavesdropper
stunts.text: On a successful Investigate roll to create an advantage by eavesdropping on a conversation, you can discover or create one additional aspect (though this doesn’t give you an extra free invocation).

stunts.name: Eye for Detail
stunts.text: Your visual memory is so strong that with a little concentration, you can revisit any place you've been to in your memory in exacting detail. Sometimes, you can even pick up on details that you hadn’t consciously realized before. To use this ability, spend a fate point and make a single perception-based roll (usually Investigate, but not necessarily limited to that) to find things out as if you were still in the location, no matter how long ago you left it.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.17.1

stunts.name: Focused Senses
stunts.text: You are skilled at concentrating on one of your senses to the exclusion of all others. The sense must be specified at the time this stunt is taken. As a free action, you may gain the Focused on My Senses aspect. So long as this aspect remains, for as long as you use nothing but Investigate, all Investigate actions you take that use the specified sense gain a +2 bonus. However, your opponents may invoke the aspect against you once for free. Rolling a skill other than Investigate removes the aspect. (This stunt may be taken multiple times, each time for a single sense. If you have specified multiple senses, your focus may cover all of them at once.)
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.17.2

stunts.name: Impossible Detail
stunts.text: When paying attention, your senses operate at a profound level of focus, allowing you to pick up on details that, very simply, no one else easily or even possibly could. With this stunt, you face no increased difficulties due to a physical detail being too small or subtle.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.17.2

stunts.name: Scene of the Crime
stunts.text: You have a strong visual memory, and whenever you revisit a place where you have used Investigate before, it takes a matter of seconds for you to use Investigate to determine what has changed since you were last there.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.17.1

stunts.name: De-Bugger
stunts.text: +2 to overcome with Investigate when you sweep a room for surveillance devices.

stunts.name: Game Hunter’s Nose
stunts.text: Choose a type of animal. You gain +2 to create advantage or overcome with Investigate when you search for or track that kind of animal.

stunts.name: Hit the Books
stunts.text: +2 to overcome or create advantage with Investigate when you seek or consult textual sources.

stunts.name: Internal Affairs
stunts.text: +2 to overcome or create advantage with Investigate when on the trail of corruption.

stunts.name: Plague Hunter
stunts.text: +2 to Investigate when you seek people with a highly infectious disease.

stunts.name: Relic Hunter
stunts.text: +2 to Investigate when you seek artefacts from ancient civilizations.

stunts.name: Tracker
stunts.text: +2 to Investigate rolls made to analyse or follow a person or creature's physical trail.

stunts.name: The Pieces of the Puzzle
stunts.text: When you take a few minutes to study a particular item and its position, you can reasonably reconstruct the chain of events that led to it being there. This reconstruction will be accurate, though it will not reveal any more than the necessary details. For example, it might reveal that it was carried by hand at some point, but not by whom.

stunts.name: The Power of Deduction
stunts.text: Once per scene you can spend a fate point (and a few minutes of observation) to make a special Investigate roll representing your potent deductive faculties. For each shift you make on this roll you discover or create an aspect, on either the scene or the target of your observations, though you may only invoke one of them for free.

stunts.name: Uncanny Hunch
stunts.text: Sometimes your guesses play out to great advantage. Once per scene, you may make a guess about what the “deal” is with a particular character, object, location, or situation. Do not speak this guess aloud; write it down on a piece of paper and give it to the GM. The GM must accept it as a valid hunch that would be something of a revelation if true (i.e., no “I’m convinced that moon orbits the Earth!” – that’s too obvious).
