If, at some later point, your hunch proves to be correct, you may use your Investigate or Empathy skill instead of any other skill, where that target is concerned, for one exchange. (A savvy GM will occasionally alter her characters’ motives to match your hunches; if she does, that’s absolutely perfect!)
stunts.requires: one other Investigate stunt and one Empathy stunt
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.17.1

stunts.name: Attention to Detail
stunts.text: You can use Investigate instead of Empathy to defend against Deceive attempts. What others discover through gut reactions and intuition, you learn through careful observation of microexpressions.

stunts.name: Going Undercover
stunts.text: Sometimes looking like someone else is just part of a detective's job. You may use Investigate in place of Deceive to create and maintain disguises or cover identities.

stunts.name: I Will Find Out What I Want To Know
stunts.text: There's not much point being able to get information from a crime scene if you can't get information from a person. You may use Investigate in place of Provoke to interrogate a suspect.

stunts.name: Investigative Reporter
stunts.text: Your writing style depends more upon good research than anything else. You may use Investigate instead of Provoke or Rapport for journalism.

stunts.name: Lip Reader
stunts.text: You may use Investigate to eavesdrop on conversations you can only see. If the GM would normally allow someone to attempt to read lips, you gain +2 to the roll; otherwise, you may simply roll Investigate when others may not.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.17.2

stunts.name: Look Behind You
stunts.text: Following a suspect is easy; doing it without their knowledge is the trick, and you've got that trick down. You may use Investigate in place of Stealth when shadowing a "person of interest".

stunts.name: Reading Suspects
stunts.text: Part of being a good detective is knowing "whodunit" long before anything can be proved. You may use Investigate in place of Empathy when you have at least one piece of evidence indicating that your target is a suspect in your current case.

stunts.name: They Don't Deserve the Truth
stunts.text: You may use Investigate in place of Deceive to lie to about a case.

stunts.name: Quick Eye
stunts.text: You are able to investigate a location much more quickly than others, while still being very thorough. All Investigate efforts you make happen one to two time increments faster than usual, allowing you to make one or two additional rolls in the same amount of time, or simply conclude your investigation faster than you would otherwise.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.17.2

stunts.name: Animal Affinity
stunts.text: Pick a particular type of animal (cats, rodents, horses or the like). At the start of any scene, if that type of animal could reasonably appear in the location where the scene is set, you may make a Lore check against a difficulty of Fair (+2). If you succeed, there is an animal of this type in the scene.

stunts.name: Animal Friend
stunts.text: Pick a particular type of animal (cats, rodents, horses or the like). You can communicate with animals of this type using a combination of speech and gestures. This doesn’t connote a special level of intelligence on the part of the animals, so the communication may be relatively simple. You also gain +2 to your rolls when interacting socially with animals of this type.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.28.1

stunts.name: Kindred Beast
stunts.text: Choose a type of animal. You gain a further +2 to create advantage or overcome when you try to calm or communicate with animals of that kind.

stunts.name: King of the Beasts
stunts.text: This stunt functions as Animal Friend does, but the character may speak to an entire broad category of animals, rather than just one type. For purposes of this ability there are three main categories – creatures from or from near the sea (fish, whales, seabirds), creatures from the land (dogs, primates, cats, birds) and vermin (bugs, rats and other small scuttling things). There is loose overlap between these categories – pigeons are in all three – and the GM is encouraged to be generous in her interpretation.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.28.1

stunts.name: Wild Empathy
stunts.text: +2 to create advantage or overcome with Lore when you try to calm or communicate with animals.

stunts.name: The Blessing of a Thousand Tongues
stunts.text: You may learn any language quickly. With tutelage, it takes only a day. With only the opportunity to read or listen, it takes a week. If the source material is especially sparse, it may take as long as a month.

stunts.name: Gift of Tongues
stunts.text: . There is no “mainstream” earthly language you cannot read or speak. Not only that, but you read and speak languages you have no business having learned, such as languages from lost cultures. You may spend a fate point to declare that you know any particular language, no matter how strange.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.2.1

stunts.name: Linguist
stunts.text: You know a wide range of languages. +2 to Lore whenever reading, writing, speaking or translating an unusual language.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.2.1

stunts.name: Shared Humanity
stunts.text: Once per scene, you can communicate a short message to another human even if you do not speak a common language.

stunts.name: Photographic Memory
stunts.text: +2 to Lore rolls whenever you lack direct access to research materials and the answer you seek lies in something you have read before.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.2.2

stunts.name: Studied Recall
stunts.text: Your photographic memory extends outside of books. Once per scene, you may spend a fate point and roll Lore against a difficulty of Mediocre. Each shift you generate may be used to specify a target that you wish to memorize as you might a book – returning later, in your mind, to assess new details (using an appropriate perception skill, usually Investigate). (This ability differs from Investigate’s Eye for Detail stunt in that Eye for Detail covers the entire location, after the fact, whereas Studied Recall requires you to specify which individual pieces of a location you are studying, while you are still in that location.)
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.2.2

stunts.name: Walking Library
stunts.text: Your prodigious reading has paid off in spades, and you are able to recall minute details from even the most obscure literary works. You don’t ever have to spend a fate point to declare that you have the proper tools for research using Lore, even in extreme situations (like being imprisoned and unable to access a library). This source of opposition is just off the table.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.2.2

stunts.name: Drinking from the Jug
stunts.text: You pause to take a swig of wine from your jug, fortifying yourself for the battle. When you have a drink during a fight, clear your lowest stress box. This requires you to take an entire action drinking.

stunts.name: Forensic Medicine
stunts.text: You can use Lore in place of Investigate when the subject involves medical evidence.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.25.1

stunts.name: Heal Thyself
stunts.text: +2 to treat your own physical consequences with Lore.

stunts.name: Herbal Remedies
stunts.text: +2 to Lore rolls related to gathering plants suitable for treating the sick or injured.

stunts.name: Plastic Surgeon
stunts.text: You know how to rearrange someone's face permanently. When you operate on a patient, you may use Lore to inflict physical stress on them. The greater the change you wish to make, the graver the consequence you must successfully inflict. (The GM decides what level of consequence is required for each change, and the consequence acts as justification for the patient to change an aspect to one relating to physical appearance at the next milestone. To alter an aspect against a character's will requires you to inflict an extreme consequence.)

stunts.name: Pouring Wine
stunts.text: You take out a cup and pour a drink from your jug. This elaborate and difficult task causes a pause in the battle. No one may attack you while you pour, and you remove your lowest stress mark. This technique requires an entire action, and you may not perform the technique more than once in a row.

stunts.name: Scholar, Healer
stunts.text: Can make physical recovery attempts with Lore.

stunts.name: Surgeon/Medical Specialist
stunts.text: You are a respected authority in a specific field of surgical or therapeutic medicine; define it at the time you take this stunt. Possibilities include heart or brain surgery, transplant operations, disease pathologies, and so on. You get a +2 to all Lore rolls relating to that field.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.25.1

stunts.name: Dizzying Intellect
stunts.text: Your area of knowledge is so advanced, there’s usually no one around who can tell if you’re making things up. You may use Lore in place of Deceive to tell lies related to your field of specialization.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.2.3

stunts.name: It's Academic
stunts.text: Once per scene you can spend a fate point (and a few minutes of observation) to make a special Lore roll representing a flash of insight. For each shift you make on this roll you discover or create an aspect related to your field of specialization, on either the scene or the target of your observations, though you may only invoke one of them for free.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.2.3

stunts.name: Secrets of the Stacks
stunts.text: Pick a specific library or other large information resource. You are intimately familiar with this resource's quirks, and gain a +2 to Lore whenever you have sufficient time to consult it.

stunts.name: Specialist
stunts.text: Choose a field of specialization, such as herbology, criminology, or zoology. You get a +2 to all Lore rolls relating to that field of specialization.

stunts.name: Tutor
stunts.text: +2 to create advantage on an ally with Lore when you spend an hour or so coaching them on an appropriate topic.

stunts.name: Caveman Lifestyle
stunts.text: You know how to live naked in the wilderness. When you undertake survival activities, you never suffer increased difficulty due to a lack of tools.

stunts.name: Due North
stunts.text: You always know which direction north is, flawlessly, even underground, without a compass or stars to guide you. You gain a +2 to Lore rolls whenever trying to find your way out of a place.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.28.2

stunts.name: Forager
stunts.text: Choose a natural habitat (e.g. forests, grasslands, deserts, oceans, or caves). You gain +2 to Lore when gathering food in that habitat.

stunts.name: Natural Dowser
stunts.text: +2 to create advantage with Lore when you seek sources of water.

stunts.name: Pathfinder
stunts.text: Navigating on foot with your Lore skill works impeded by poor visibility or difficult terrain.

stunts.name: Scout the Path
stunts.text: +2 to create advantage with Lore when blazing a trail through the wilderness.

stunts.name: Self-Sufficient
stunts.text: You don’t ever have to spend a fate point to declare that you are able to find enough food and water for yourself, even in extreme situations (like being dumped in the middle of the desert and separated from all your stuff). This source of opposition is just off the table.

stunts.name: Advanced Ritualist
stunts.text: You gain a +2 bonus when you use Lore in place of another skill during a challenge. This allows you to use Lore twice in the same challenge.

stunts.name: Actions Speak Louder Than Words
stunts.text: Dealing with animals, who don't talk, has given you an excellent grasp of body language. You may use your Lore skill instead of Empathy to defend against attempts to attack or create advantage with Deceive.

stunts.name: Animal Magnetism
stunts.text: It's a bit demeaning to equate seduction to animal training, but in your experience there isn't all that much difference between the two activities. You may use Lore instead of Provoke to seduce people.

stunts.name: Cracker
stunts.text: You may use Lore in place of Burglary to defeat computerised security.

stunts.name: Formal Logic/Master of Riddles
stunts.text: Your intelligence lets you run circles around those you talk to. This may take the form of actual riddles, or perhaps just complex logical arguments. You may use Lore to make attacks that inflict mental stress and to create advantages related to confusing and overaweing people. Such actions can be defended against with Rapport, Lore, or Empathy.

stunts.name: Frontiersmen Have To Improvise
stunts.text: Making stuff out of the things around you is an integral part of wilderness survival. You may use Lore in place of Crafts to build things out of scavenged materials.

stunts.name: Outdoorsman
stunts.text: Your extensive field experience helps you operate in the wild. You may roll Lore instead of Stealth whenever you are in the wilderness, and may also roll Lore instead of Investigate for tracking in those areas.

stunts.name: Pre-Prepared Counterpoint
stunts.text: You’ve heard that argument before, and you know how to defeat it. You may use Lore to defend against Rapport.

stunts.name: Professional Teacher
stunts.text: You may use Lore in place of Rapport to interact with your students.

stunts.name: Ritualist
stunts.text: Use Lore in place of another skill during a challenge, allowing you to use Lore twice in the same challenge.

stunts.name: Shield of Reason
stunts.text: You can use Lore as a defense against Provoke attempts, provided you can justify your ability to overcome your fear through rational thought and reason.

stunts.name: Theory in Practice
stunts.text: Once per scene you can spend a fate point to use Lore in place of any other skill for one roll.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.25.2

stunts.name: They're In the Trees
stunts.text: Basic wilderness survival includes a great deal of stealth. You may use Lore in place of Stealth as long as you are outdoors.

stunts.name: Well-Travelled
stunts.text: You may use Lore instead of Rapport when you have visited the homeland or home state of the person you are speaking to.

stunts.name: Arcane Expert
stunts.text: Gain a +2 bonus to create an advantage using Lore, whenever the situation has specifically to do with the supernatural or occult.

stunts.name: Bletchley's Finest
stunts.text: +2 to overcome with Lore when cracking a code.

stunts.name: Dealer in Antiquities
stunts.text: +2 to create advantages with Lore based on the monetary value of archaeological finds.

stunts.name: Experimenter
stunts.text: While others are content to read the journals, you have the training and drive to perform cutting-edge research. +2 to Lore whenever you run original scientific experiments or gather original research data.

stunts.name: The Eye Sees All Paths
stunts.text: You may not know everything, but you always know how to find out. When looking for a fairly specific piece of information, you may give the GM a fate point to be told the closest place you can go to find out, no matter how obscure or lost the information is. In short, you can never hit a wall when trying to find something out. There are no guarantees of how easy it will be to get the knowledge, but that’s what adventure is for.

stunts.name: I’ve Read about That!
stunts.text: You’ve read hundreds—if not thousands—of books on a wide variety of topics. You can spend a fate point to use Lore in place of any other skill for one roll or exchange, provided you can justify having read about the action you’re attempting.

stunts.name: Keeper of Folklore
stunts.text: +2 to Lore when recalling the history or legends of your people.

stunts.name: Legal Eagle
stunts.text: +2 to overcome or create an advantage with Lore, whenever you are finding or exploiting loopholes in the law.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.18.2

stunts.name: Meteorologist
stunts.text: You are trained as a meteorologist and so you are skilled at weather prediction. +2 to Lore when creating advantages to do with the weather.

stunts.name: World Court
stunts.text: Your exposure to international law is so extensive that you’re at ease in any situation involving legal wrangling, wherever you are. You never suffer any increased difficulty from a lack of familiarity with the laws of your locale; your experience is so broad that you’ve either know it already, or can make highly educated guesses about how it functions.

stunts.name: On Top Of It
stunts.text: You may spend a fate point to go first in an exchange, regardless of your Notice. If multiple people with this stunt exercise this ability, they go in turn based on their skills, before those who don’t exercise the stunt get a chance to act. If the exchange has already started, and you have not yet acted, you may instead spend a fate point to act next, out of the usual turn order.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.3.1

stunts.name: Ready for Anything
stunts.text: Your senses are so keyed into minute changes that you are able to respond more quickly to new details. Your Notice is considered to be one higher for purposes of determining turn order. This stunt breaks ties whenever facing opponents with the same Notice. This stunt may be taken multiple times, each time increasing the character’s effective Notice by 1.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.3.1

stunts.name: Run Interference
stunts.text: Whenever it is determined that you provide active opposition to another character's action, you may spend a fate point. When you do, the other character may choose to attempt another action instead. If they do not, you receive +2 on your defend roll against the original action.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.3.1

stunts.name: Constant Vigilance
stunts.text: When you are ambushed, gain a further +2 to the first defend roll you make.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.3.2

stunts.name: Danger Sense
stunts.text: You have an almost preternatural capacity for detecting danger. Your Notice skill works unimpeded by conditions like total concealment, darkness, or other sensory impairments in situations where someone or something intends to harm you.

stunts.name: Saw It Coming
stunts.text: When you are ambushed, gain +2 to any defend rolls you make in the first exchange.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.3.2

stunts.name: The Eye Gazes in All Directions
stunts.text: You are never surprised. Even if it’s only by a moment, you are always forewarned of the unexpected.

stunts.name: Sentry
stunts.text: You have the ability to wait, devoting your full effort to watchfulness, for hours on end. +2 to defend with Notice whenever you are tired.

stunts.name: Take It All In
stunts.text: Once per scene you can spend a fate point (and a few minutes of observation) to make a special Notice roll representing opening your senses to a location. For each shift you make on this roll you discover or create an aspect related to direct observation on the scene, though you may only invoke one of them for free.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.3.2

stunts.name: Body Language Reader
stunts.text: You can use Notice in place of Empathy to learn the aspects of a target through observation.

stunts.name: Master of the Tell
stunts.text: Long practice has made you incomparably good at noticing the mannerisms that accompany deception. +2 to Notice when using it to defend against Deceive.

stunts.name: Notice Tell
stunts.text: Your keen senses allow you to pick up on the subtle clues that indicate when a person is lying. You may use Notice to defend against Deceive.

stunts.name: Reactive Shot
stunts.text: You can use Notice instead of Shoot to make quick, reactive shots that don’t involve a lot of aiming. However, because you’re having a knee-jerk reaction, you’re not allowed to concretely identify your target before using this stunt. So, for example, you might be able to shoot at someone you see moving in the bushes with this stunt, but you won’t be able to tell if it’s friend or foe before you pull the trigger. Choose carefully!

stunts.name: The Advantage of Familiarity
stunts.text: There are benefits to knowing a place really well. Pick a location or a small neighbourhood. +2 to Notice while you are in that area.

stunts.name: Attention!
stunts.text: You have been trained to follow orders instantly in combat. When determining turn order for a physical conflict, you may use an ally's Notice skill instead of your own.

stunts.name: Game Hunter’s Eye
stunts.text: Choose a type of animal. You gain +2 to create advantage or overcome with Notice to spot that kind of animal.

stunts.name: Heightened Awareness
stunts.text: +2 to defend with Notice during a physical conflict.

stunts.name: Hidey-Holes
stunts.text: +2 to create advantage with Notice based on finding a suitable location to stay hidden.

stunts.name: Keen Sense
stunts.text: Choose a physical sense (e.g. sight, hearing, touch, taste, smell). You gain +2 to defend or overcome with Notice when that sense is the primary one being used.

stunts.name: Recognise Imposter
stunts.text: +2 to overcome with Notice when faced someone claiming to be a celebrity or someone you know well.

stunts.name: Always Healthy/Strong Immune System
stunts.text: +2 to overcome rolls with Physique to resist disease.

stunts.name: Death Defiance
stunts.text: If you are taken out in a physical conflict, you may spend a fate point to concede instead. After you have collected fate points for conceding, you must spend a further amount of half of your fate points, rounded down. Coincidence conspires to keep you alive, and you pass from the view of the other combatants (such as by dropping off a cliff, apparently failing to escape from an exploding building, or the like). You may re-enter play in any subsequent scene in as dramatic a fashion as you see fit, explaining to everyone how you survived. You return with all of your physical stress cleared and a single additional consequence incurred to reflect the dangers you defied.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.11.2

stunts.name: Desertborn
stunts.text: +2 to overcome or defend with Physique against heat and thirst.

stunts.name: Developed Immunities
stunts.text: You gain a further +2 to overcome rolls with Physique to resist any poison you have previously encountered "on screen".
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.11.2

stunts.name: Large Lung Capacity
stunts.text: +2 to Physique to overcome or defend against suffocation or drowning.

stunts.name: Last Leg
stunts.text: You may spend fate points to keep standing. Any time you would suffer a consequence or be taken out by physical stress, you may spend a fate point to remain standing or otherwise defer a consequence for one more exchange, or until you take stress again, whichever comes first. Once the extra time you've bought is up, all the effects you have deferred come to bear at once. You may keep spending fate points each time the time limit expires until you run out. (This makes it possible for you to be taken out by a character who has already conceded or been taken out in the intervening time!)
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.11.1

stunts.name: Tireless
stunts.text: +2 to Physique when rolling to overcome or defend against exhaustion or sleep deprivation.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.11.1

stunts.name: Toxin Exposure
stunts.text: +2 to overcome rolls with Physique to resist poisons.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.11.2

stunts.name: Body Toss
stunts.text: You know how to apply your strength in a fight to take people off their feet. +2 to create advantages with Physique whenever you try to throw or push someone.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.19.2

stunts.name: Domino Effect
stunts.text: When you succeed with style on an attempt to push over or trip an opponent, you may create an additional identical aspect on another weaker opponent in the same zone. Both aspects come with one free invocation. (“Weaker opponent” here means an opponent with a lower Physique than the one who defended against your action.)

stunts.name: The Drunken Shove
stunts.text: Your rude and artless push contains a greater power than seems possible. You gain +2 to use Physique to create an advantage on an opponent by knocking them off balance.

stunts.name: Low Centre of Gravity
stunts.text: +2 to defend with Physique against attempts to trip or grapple you.

stunts.name: Scrum
stunts.text: You may roll Physique to push yourself and an opponent into an adjacent zone, provided there are no situation aspects impeding movement. Your opponent may defend with either Athletics or Physique.

stunts.name: Face the Pain
stunts.text: You are able to lessen the effects of physical injury thanks to your incredible stamina. Once per scene, you may spend a fate point, and uncheck any one of your physical stress boxes.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.11.1

stunts.name: Feel the Burn
stunts.text: You can push through incredible pain in order to reach your goal. You gain an additional mild consequence slot. This slot can only be used for physical harm.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.11.1

stunts.name: Man of Iron
stunts.text: When you take physical stress, and the stress box with a value equal to the shift value of the hit is already checked, you may instead mark the next lowest value box that is unchecked. Very simply, this means that you don’t start picking up consequences unless someone hits you for more than your highest value box (difficult at best!) or all of your boxes are filled up.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.11.3

stunts.name: One Hit to the Body
stunts.text: When you take physical stress, you may check off two stress boxes with a total value equal to or greater than the shift value of the hit.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.11.3

stunts.name: Thick Skinned
stunts.text: You gain one more physical stress box.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.11.3

stunts.name: Tough as Nails
stunts.text: Once per session, at the cost of a fate point, you can reduce the severity of a moderate consequence that’s physical in nature to a mild consequence (if your mild consequence slot is free), or erase a mild consequence altogether.

stunts.name: Grappler
stunts.text: +2 to Physique rolls made to create advantages on an enemy by wrestling or grappling with them.

stunts.name: Hammerlock
stunts.text: Whenever you have hold of someone and they fail to overcome your hold, you deal 1 shift of physical stress to them.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.19.2

stunts.name: Unbound/Clever Wrestling
stunts.text: You aren't easy to hold down. +2 to overcome with Physique whenever you are physically restrained in some fashion - for example by chains or a mob of people.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.19.1, and http://dfrpg-resources.wikispaces.com/Stunts

stunts.name: Bounce Back
stunts.text: You may roll Physique instead of Lore when performing a physical recovery action on yourself.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.11.2

stunts.name: Fling Foe
stunts.text: You may roll Physique to throw an enemy you have Picked Up into an adjacent zone. You must overcome any situation aspects that impede the enemy’s movement.

stunts.name: Heavy Object Swing
stunts.text: Sometimes pure strength can compensate pretty well for a lack of skill. You may use Physique instead of Fight whenever you use a heavy object as a melee weapon.

stunts.name: Heavy Object Throw
stunts.text: If you spin a weight fast enough, it can become airborne. You may use Physique instead of Shoot to attack targets one zone away with a heavy object.

stunts.name: Mighty Pull
stunts.text: You can use Physique to create advantages related to your ability to draw bows back further than most, granting extra force to the arrow or bolt.

stunts.name: Muscle Your Way Up
stunts.text: Climbing is basically like weightlifting, except you are the weight. You may use Physique in place of Athletics when climbing.

stunts.name: Piledriver
stunts.text: You may make attacks against inanimate targets using Physique instead of Fight.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.19.1

stunts.name: Shield Sling
stunts.text: When armed with a shield, you may attack an opponent one zone away with Physique, but doing so places the aspect No Shield on you.

stunts.name: Take the Blow
stunts.text: You can use Physique to defend against Fight attacks made with fists or blunt instruments, though you always take 1 shift of stress on a tie.

stunts.name: Toughness of Mind and Body
stunts.text: A guy as tough as you has no need to be afraid. You may use Physique instead of Will to defend against fear.

stunts.name: Unstoppable
stunts.text: Once in motion, you are very difficult to stop due to your sheer muscular force. You may use Physique rather than Athletics to move between zones.
stunts.requires: Herculean Strength and at least one other Physique stunt
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.19.1

stunts.name: Wrestler/Power Over Finesse
stunts.text: Your unarmed attacks rely on brute strength rather than on technique. You may make such attacks against other humans with Physique rather than Fight.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.19.2, and http://dfrpg-resources.wikispaces.com/Stunts

stunts.name: Bend Bars, Lift Gates
stunts.text: You may spend a fate point to automatically overcome a Physique obstacle, even if you’ve already rolled for it, provided you’re trying to accomplish something through brute strength.

stunts.name: Charge Like Ox
stunts.text: Because you are Strong Like Ox, once per scene, as a single action, you may move two zones in a straight line then make a physical attack.

stunts.name: Favored Enemy Tackle
stunts.text: Choose an organisation. You gain +2 to create advantage with Physique against members of that group.

stunts.name: Give As Good As I Get
stunts.text: Sometimes you have to do something crazy in order to win a fight. Once per conflict, when you take physical stress, you may choose to incur an additional physical consequence. In exchange, you may create a situation aspect on your opponent with a number of free invocations: two for a minor consequence, three for a moderate, four for a severe.

stunts.name: Herculean Strength
stunts.text: +2 to overcome or create advantage rolls with Physique that involve lifting great weights.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.19.1

stunts.name: Hulking Rage
stunts.text: While you have the aspect Enraged on you, you gain +2 to overcome and create advantage with Physique.

stunts.name: None Shall Pass
stunts.text: +2 to defend with Physique against attempts to move past you.

stunts.name: Now You've Made Me Mad
stunts.text: Once per scene, after taking physical stress, you may spend a fate point to add the shift value of the attack (after any reduction by consequences) as a bonus to an action in the next exchange taken against the person who inflicted the stress.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.11.3

stunts.name: Smashing Rage
stunts.text: While you have the aspect Enraged on you, you gain +2 to break inanimate objects with Physique.

stunts.name: Trample
stunts.text: Once per scene, when you succeed with style on a create advantage roll with Physique and place an aspect on an opponent, you may exchange one of your free invocations for a 2-shift hit on that opponent.

stunts.name: Aura of Fear
stunts.text: Your intimidating appearance and attitude are potent, making you able to intimidate entire crowds. Once per scene, you may spend a fate point and make an intimidation attempt against all opponents in the scene. If you succeed, attach an aspect representing the intimidation to each opponent. (This doesn't get you any additional free invocations of these aspects.)
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.16.2

stunts.name: Aura of Menace
stunts.text: You are the terror of all those who oppose you. Once per scene per target, you may spend a fate point to intimidate a target as a free action, no matter what the circumstances, immediately (if between actions), or immediately after the current action underway.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.16.2

stunts.name: Crown of Menace
stunts.text: You are too terrifying to be attacked. Until you make a physical attack in a scene, characters with a Will lower than Good (+3) simply cannot attack you. Those with sufficient Will to attack still flinch on their first attack, though, automatically missing.

stunts.name: Daunting Presence
stunts.text: +2 to create advantages similar to Daunted with Provoke.

stunts.name: Fearsome Gaze
stunts.text: Your gaze is so terrifying that those faced with it can end up paralyzed with fear. This stunt is used in the same fashion as Steely Gaze, but if your opponent loses to the point of taking a consequence, he takes other consequences immediately afterwards. Even if this means he’s taken out, the target retains the option to concede after recording the consequence.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.16.2

stunts.name: Master of Fear
stunts.text: You are a master of the terrifying, and can have an entire room cowering within moments. Nameless NPCs who are affected by your Aura of Fear are automatically taken out; they simply flee or faint.
stunts.requires: Fearsome Gaze and Aura of Fear
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.16.2

stunts.name: Menacing Demeanor
stunts.text: When you are face-to-face with another person, gain +2 to create advantages specifically related to fear on them with Provoke.

stunts.name: Subtle Menace
stunts.text: You exude menace far in excess of your capability to act. Even bound and behind prison bars, you are so ripe with the promise of the awful things you could do that you're still scary. +2 to Provoke rolls when opposed by someone in a clearly superior position of power.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.16.1

stunts.name: Berserk Rage
stunts.text: When you suffer a physical consequence, you can invoke that consequence for free on your next attack. If you suffer multiple physical consequences, you get a free invocation for each.

stunts.name: Infuriate
stunts.text: Sometimes fear isn’t an option, but that doesn’t mean you can’t still get up someone’s nose. +2 to Provoke rolls whenever deliberately trying to get someone angry with you.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.16.1

stunts.name: Master of Mockery
stunts.text: When you place an aspect such as Enraged with <Your Name Here> on an opponent, that opponent can do nothing but attack you until the aspect is overcome.

stunts.name: Poison Words
stunts.text: Your skill at satire is so profound that you can take a whole audience with you. During a satirical performance, advantages you create with Provoke attach to each character present. You choose to which person your free invocations apply.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.4.3

stunts.name: Razor Tongue
stunts.text: You know how to craft the most exquisite insults. +2 to create advantage with Provoke whenever you eloquently insult a rival.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.4.3

stunts.name: Teflon Troublemaker
stunts.text: When your Can’t Keep His Big Mouth Shut aspect is compelled to make you the target of an attack, you may immediately clear any mild consequences you currently have, instead of taking a fate point.

stunts.name: Ladies' Man/Popular Gal
stunts.text: You’re adept at catching the eye of the opposite sex, and keeping it once you’ve got it. Any seduction attempts you make with Provoke receive a +2 bonus whenever the target is someone who could be receptive to it (this is not always a simple case of gender and preference).
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.22.1

stunts.name: Armor of Fear
stunts.text: You can use Provoke to defend against Fight attacks, but only until the first time you’re dealt stress in a conflict. You can make your opponents hesitate to attack, but when someone shows them that you’re only human your advantage disappears.

stunts.name: The Fight in the Dog
stunts.text: You can use Provoke to enter the kinds of contests that you’d normally need Physique for, whenever your ability to psych your opponent out with the force of your presence alone would be a factor.

stunts.name: Imposing Attitude
stunts.text: For some reason, people seem reluctant to disagree with you. Maybe it’s your cologne. You may use Provoke instead of Rapport to defend attempts to damage your reputation.

stunts.name: Okay, Fine!
stunts.text: You can use Provoke in place of Empathy to learn a target’s aspects, by bullying them until they reveal one to you. The target defends against this with Will. (If the GM thinks the aspect is particularly vulnerable to your hostile approach, you get a +2 bonus.)

stunts.name: Scary
stunts.text: You are just someone people don’t want to cross, and that’s clear even to other intimidating folks. You may use Provoke instead of Will to defend against Provoke.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.16.2

stunts.name: The Serpent's Tongue
stunts.text: It’s hard not to talk to you. Not because you're approachable, but because it seems like such a bad idea not to. Fear makes people uncomfortable, and they occasionally let things slip they would not otherwise. You may use Provoke in place of Empathy or Rapport when trying to get information out of someone in a “softer” fashion. If successfully used in this way, the target is definitely rattled – so it certainly doesn’t leave the target in the same pleasant state he might be left by one of those other skills. If used to read a character's emotional state, the aspects revealed are limited only to those which might be expressed in the language of fear.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.16.1

stunts.name: Tell Me or Else!
stunts.text: You don't ask nicely when there's stuff you need to know. You may roll Provoke instead of Contacts when you are gathering information from your informants.

stunts.name: Unapproachable
stunts.text: It’s difficult to try to manipulate someone when you’re constantly reminded of how scary they are. You may use Provoke instead of Will to provide defend against create advantage actions made with Deceive, Empathy, or Rapport.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.16.1

stunts.name: Bad Cop
stunts.text: Cruelty is more effective when given a basis for comparison. Once per scene, gain +2 to Provoke when invoking an aspect created by someone who has the Good Cop stunt.

stunts.name: Berate the Underlings
stunts.text: +2 to create advantage or attack with Provoke when you interact with your subordinates.

stunts.name: Favored Enemy Rattle
stunts.text: Choose an organisation. You gain +2 to attack or create advantage with Provoke against members of that group.

stunts.name: Not to Be Trifled With
stunts.text: When you make it clear how dangerous you are, roll Provoke against your target’s Will. If you succeed, that target will not attack you or willingly come near you unless you take action against him first. If you succeed with style, neither will anyone with a lower Will than your target.

stunts.name: Provoke Violence
stunts.text: When you create an advantage on an opponent using Provoke, you can use your free invocation to become the target of that character’s next relevant action, drawing their attention away from another target.

stunts.name: Scare 'Em Straight
stunts.text: You are an authority figure. Part of your job is to put the fear of the law in potential miscreants. +2 to Provoke when using it to frighten someone under your authority (e.g. students for a teacher).

stunts.name: The Promise of Pain
stunts.text: Once per conflict, you can force the opponent to use a mild consequence instead of a 2-point stress box on a successful Provoke attack.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.16.2

stunts.name: Steely Gaze
stunts.text: Your unflinching gaze can lock an opponent in place. When you look an opponent in the eyes and successfully create an advantage with Provoke, both of you can only take Provoke actions against each other until one of you takes a consequence, concedes, or is interrupted (by, say, a gunshot).
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.16.2

stunts.name: Street Talk
stunts.text: +2 to Provoke when dealing with the inhabitants of slums.

stunts.name: Torturer
stunts.text: You have the complete lack of mercy that is needed to torture someone properly. Once per scene, when you force an opponent to take a consequence instead of mental stress, you can spend a fate point to increase the consequence’s severity (so mild becomes moderate, moderate becomes severe). If your opponent was already going to take a severe consequence, he must either take a severe consequence and a second consequence or be taken out.

stunts.name: Wounds From a Friend
stunts.text: It's hard to disbelieve what those closest to you tell you. While successfully impersonating someone, your successful Provoke attacks on their close associates inflict two additional stress.

stunts.name: Do You Know Who I Am?
stunts.text: Once per scene, you may identify yourself in order to get your way and add +2 to a Contacts, Deceive, Provoke, or Rapport roll.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.4.4

stunts.name: Moving Performance
stunts.text: When you create an advantage with Rapport using your art, the difficulty of removing the resulting aspect increases by +2.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.4.2

stunts.name: Stage Presence
stunts.text: +2 to overcome distractions with Rapport while performing.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.4.3

stunts.name: Virtuoso/Artist
stunts.text: Choose a field of art, such as painting, composition, or singing. You get a +2 to all Rapport rolls relating to that art.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.4.2

stunts.name: Demagogue
stunts.text: +2 to Rapport when you’re delivering an inspiring speech in front of a crowd. (If there are named NPCs or PCs in the scene, you may target them all simultaneously with one roll rather than dividing up your shifts.)

stunts.name: Excellent Speaker
stunts.text: Public speaking is an everyday thing to you. +2 to Rapport whenever you make a formal speech to a group.

stunts.name: Another Round?
stunts.text: +2 to Rapport when drinking with someone in a tavern.

stunts.name: Blood is Thicker Than Water
stunts.text: +2 to Rapport when dealing with members of your extended family.

stunts.name: Captain’s Word
stunts.text: Once per scene, you may roll Rapport to command your crew as a free action.

stunts.name: Child of the Court
stunts.text: Gain a +2 bonus to any attempt to overcome obstacles with Rapport when you’re at an aristocratic function, such as a royal ball.

stunts.name: Good Cop
stunts.text: Kindness is more effective when given a basis for comparison. +2 to Rapport when creating advantages to assist someone who has the Bad Cop stunt.

stunts.name: Honest Salesman
stunts.text: Making a sale comes as naturally to you as breathing. +2 to Rapport when using it to sell goods or services.

stunts.name: Master of the Mob
stunts.text: +2 to Rapport when dealing with a crowd or mob.

stunts.name: Negotiator
stunts.text: +2 to Rapport when you try to broker an end to an armed conflict.

stunts.name: Scion of the Court
stunts.text: When you overcome an obstacle with Child of the Court, you may additionally create a situation aspect that describes how the general attitude turns in your favor. If anyone wants to try and get rid of this aspect, they must overcome Fair (+2) opposition.

stunts.name: Target Audience
stunts.text: Pick a specific field of endeavour, such as crime, business, politics, espionage, or the occult. Gain +2 to Rapport rolls whenever dealing with someone from that field.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.7.2

stunts.name: All the World's a Stage/Playing to Expectations
stunts.text: Your acting talent is natural and unquestionable. You may roll Rapport instead of Deceive when convincing a target you are someone you aren't.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.4.3

stunts.name: Animal Whisperer
stunts.text: You may use Rapport instead of Lore to issue commands to animals.

stunts.name: Blather
stunts.text: It’s not that you’re a good liar – possibly far from it. It’s more that you have a skill at talking so fast, and not letting the other guy get a word in edgewise, that he doesn’t ever get the chance to figure out if you’re lying or not. You may create an aspect such as Blathering on yourself which justifies active opposition to Alertness rolls in your zone. You cannot take other actions while blathering, but you may spend a fate point to negate any successful roll that overcomes the aspect. The targets of this effort are by no means helpless – if they are attacked or otherwise disturbed they may respond normally, and they will respond to obvious stimuli (friends being attacked in their line of sight, fire alarms going off and such). However, they are definitely distracted. Once you stop talking, it may be time for a quick exit.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.22.2

stunts.name: Commissions
stunts.text: Your works and performances are heavily sought out, and there are those who will pay handsomely for it. Once per session, you may use Rapport in place of Resources for one roll, representing a successful past commission.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.4.4

stunts.name: Large Ham
stunts.text: You may use Rapport in place of Provoke to intimidate someone.

stunts.name: Popular
stunts.text: If you’re in an area where you’re popular and well-liked, you can use Rapport in place of Contacts. You may be able to establish your popularity by spending a fate point to declare a story detail, or because of prior justification.

stunts.name: The Right Questions
stunts.text: Smaller parts of a larger truth can contain a blueprint of the whole – and as a skilled conversationalist, you are adept at pulling the larger truth out of a single individual. Provided the person you’re talking to is at least neutral towards you, you may use your Rapport skill instead of Contacts for any effort to network. The results are limited and colored by the knowledge available to the person with whom you speak.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.22.2

stunts.name: Weight of Reputation
stunts.text: For a fate point, you may use Empathy in place of Contacts, Deceive or Provoke, provided those you are dealing with are aware of your reputation.
stunts.requires: Do You Know Who I Am?
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.4.4

stunts.name: All Things in Their Place
stunts.text: You always know the power dynamic in the room, and you may insert yourself within it anywhere you desire. Use this with caution—while it impacts how people interact with you, it does not equate to actual authority, and placing yourself too highly—especially over people not used to being anything but top dog—can inspire an unpleasant response.

stunts.name: Best Foot Forward
stunts.text: Twice per session, you may upgrade a boost you receive with Rapport into a full situation aspect with a free invocation.

stunts.name: First Impressions
stunts.text: Whenever an opponent succeeds with style against the first Rapport roll you make in a scene, they do not gain a boost.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.22.1

stunts.name: Five Minutes Friends
stunts.text: For a fate point, you can make a steadfast friend in a place you’ve never been, given a chance for five minutes of conversation. This stunt makes nearly impossible opportunities to make friends merely improbable, improbable opportunities probable, and probable opportunities outright certain.

stunts.name: Heart on My Sleeve
stunts.text: You’re a regular stand up guy with no secrets, at least so far as anyone can tell. But even so, you’re in control of which part of your best face you’re putting forward. +2 to defend with Rapport against attempts to read your emotional state.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.22.2

stunts.name: International
stunts.text: Your mastery of etiquette leaves you comfortable, and even glib, in any situation. You never suffer any increased difficulty from unfamiliarity with your setting, making it easy to maneuver through local customs you haven’t encountered before, and to cover up any gaffes with a laugh and a sparkle in your eye.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.22.1

stunts.name: Rustic Charm
stunts.text: You suffer no increased difficulty on Rapport rolls due to your social class.

stunts.name: Smooth Over
stunts.text: You’re adept at stepping into a bad situation and dialing it down to something more reasonable. So long as you are not the direct reason someone is upset, your attempts to calm them down using your Rapport receive a +2 bonus.

stunts.name: Grease the Wheels
stunts.text: You can use Resources instead of Rapport in any situation where bribes will be accepted.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.24.1

stunts.name: Help Wanted, Reward Offered
stunts.text: You can use Resources instead of Contacts whenever you make it public exactly what or who you are looking for.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.24.1

stunts.name: Glitterati
stunts.text: Money can, in fact, buy friends. You may use Resources in place of Contacts when in high society.

stunts.name: Instant Functionary
stunts.text: You’re skilled at seeing the shape of an organization from the underside, and in organizations of sufficient size, you can easily convince anyone that you’re just another cog in the machine. This allows you to substitute your Resources skill for Deceive whenever pretending to fill the role of a minor functionary of a target organization.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.18.3

stunts.name: Money Talks
stunts.text: You can use Resources instead of Rapport in any situation where ostentatious displays of material wealth might aid your cause.

stunts.name: My Wallet Has A Lot To Say
stunts.text: +2 to Resources whenever you use the Money Talks stunt.

stunts.name: War of Papers
stunts.text: You can take action against organizations through indirect measures. Effectively you can fight on the level of any organization smaller than a nation without the need to recruit allies or have any organization of your own. Yes, this means you can effectively “kill” a city, or even an army, given enough time.

stunts.name: Best That Money Can Buy
stunts.text: You have a discerning taste and a natural instinct for spending your money to get exactly the best and nothing less. You are at +2 to your Resources whenever making a purchase of something that would be considered “the best.” While this may seem like a discount, it’s not, really, since seeking out the best may mandate a price mark several steps above the baseline; still, this stunt helps to soften the blow.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.24.3

stunts.name: Long Term Investment
stunts.text: You’ve had your money for a while now, and you’ve had a chance to make several strategic investments which you can cash in on when pressed for money. Once per session, you may sell one of these investments to get a +2 to any one Resources roll.

stunts.name: Licenses for Everything
stunts.text: You suffer no increased penalties on Resources rolls related to legal restrictions on goods.

stunts.name: Money Is No Object
stunts.text: Once per session, when called on to roll Resources, you may spend a fate point and simply act as if you had rolled +4 on the dice. You may do this after the fact on a roll. Your Resources skill will then operate at -2 for the rest of the session; you’ve simply tapped into everything at your disposal to make the purchase.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.24.3

stunts.name: Rivers of Gold
stunts.text: Money is just a detail to you. Stripped naked and cast on a desert island, and you’ll be living in luxury in short order. Cast into prison, and you’ll be bribing guards in no time. No situation will restrict your access to your Resources skill.

stunts.name: Savvy Investor
stunts.text: You get an additional free invoke when you create advantages with Resources, provided that they describe a monetary return on an investment you made in a previous session. (In other words, you can’t retroactively declare that you did it, but if it happened in the course of play, you get higher returns.)

stunts.name: Trust Fund Baby
stunts.text: Twice per session, you may take a boost representing a windfall or influx of cash.

stunts.name: Useful Little Things
stunts.text: Your pockets are full of useful little things. Whenever you need something, you have it, provided it’s not something too unusual (like a map to Jimmy Hoffa’s body) or too large to fit in a pocket, belt pouch, or backpack. When you say you have something, the GM should be likely to agree.

stunts.name: Wholesale Pricing
stunts.text: Pick a type of business (e.g. supermarket, sporting goods, electronics). You gain +2 to Resources when you attempt to purchase something which that business sells.

stunts.name: Scope User
stunts.text: You know how to use a scope. +2 to create advantages with Shoot related to aiming while using a scope or laser sight.

stunts.name: Uncanny Accuracy
stunts.text: Once per conflict, stack an additional free invoke on an advantage you’ve created to represent the time you take to aim or line up a shot (like In My Sights).

stunts.name: Fast Reload
stunts.text: +2 to Shoot whenever you roll to overcome an aspect of Out of Ammunition or similar that has been placed upon you.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.15.2

stunts.name: Lead in the Air
stunts.text: You really like emptying magazines. Any time you’re using a fully automatic weapon and you succeed at a Shoot attack, you automatically create a Fair (+2) opposition against movement in that zone until your next turn, because of all the lead in the air. (Normally, you’d need to take a separate action to set up this kind of interference, but with the stunt, it’s free.)

stunts.name: One Shot Left (or Empty Mag, Empty Room)
stunts.text: That last bullet has a kind of magic to it. Once per scene, you may create an aspect of One Shot Left (equivalently, The Whole Magazine at Once) on yourself as a free action. You may invoke this aspect once for free, but doing so changes the aspect to Out of Ammunition. The Fast Reload stunt explicitly cannot be used to overcome this aspect.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.15.2, and http://dfrpg-resources.wikispaces.com/Stunts

stunts.name: Rain of Lead
stunts.text: +2 to create advantage rolls with Shoot when you create an aspect relating to suppressive fire.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.15.2

stunts.name: Crazy Ricochet
stunts.text: When you use the Ricochet stunt, you may invoke further aspects to represent further bounces, gaining a bonus for each as normal.

stunts.name: Fortunate Rebound/Through and Through
stunts.text: Once per scene, when you succeed with style on a Shoot attack, you may inflict a 2-shift physical hit on another opponent in the same zone instead of gaining a boost.

stunts.name: Ricochet
stunts.text: You may invoke a relevant situation aspect to bounce a projectile off a solid surface, allowing it to come at an opponent from an unexpected direction. (This invocation does not provide its normal bonus.) If your attack is successful, the stress of the hit is increased by 2.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.29.2

stunts.name: Good Arm
stunts.text: You have an amazing throwing arm, and can throw weapons with great force. If thrown weapons have a shorter range in your game than guns, this stunt extends that range to two zones, equal to that of guns.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.29.2

stunts.name: Legendary Archer
stunts.text: Bows are not just weapons, they're your weapons of choice. When wielding a bow or crossbow, you can make attacks with it from two additional zones away.

stunts.name: Long Shot
stunts.text: You can make physical attacks with Shoot from up to three zones away, rather than the usual two.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.15.1

stunts.name: Sniper
stunts.text: Once per scene, you may make an attack with Shoot from up to ten zones away, provided you have a sniper rifle and scope.

stunts.name: Feller of Fauna
stunts.text: To you, guns aren't for killing people; they're for killing animals. +2 to Shoot attacks against mundane animals.

stunts.name: Game Hunter’s Finger
stunts.text: Choose a type of animal. You gain +2 to attack with Shoot against that kind of animal.

stunts.name: Trick Shot
stunts.text: +2 to create advantage with Shoot when firing at an inanimate object.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.15.1

stunts.name: Gun-Crazy/Way of the Gun
stunts.text: You may use Shoot instead of Crafts whenever you're working with guns specifically.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.15.4

stunts.name: Gun Kata
stunts.text: You are light on your feet with a gun in your hand, able to keep the gunplay going while evading attempts to harm you. You may use Shoot instead of Athletics to defend against physical attacks.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.15.1

stunts.name: Juggler
stunts.text: You have a great talent for juggling; this includes the ability to throw around seemingly dangerous objects (knives, torches) without any fear of harm to yourself. +2 to Shoot when using juggling to entertain.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.26.2

stunts.name: Personal Arsenal
stunts.text: You own a great number of weapons, and you get new ones all the time. Use your Shoot skill instead of your Resources skill when dealing with weaponry.

stunts.name: Quick on the Draw
stunts.text: You can use Shoot instead of Notice to determine turn order in any physical conflict where shooting quickly would be useful.

stunts.name: Shot on the Run
stunts.text: Once per scene, you may move one zone, attack with Shoot, and then move one additional zone, provided there are no situation aspects restricting movement.

stunts.name: Snap Shot
stunts.text: Once per conflict, between or before other characters’ actions, you may spend a fate point to preempt the usual turn order and act next. The action taken must involve a roll with your Shoot skill – usually an attack. This may be done in addition to your normal action.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.15.3

stunts.name: Called Shot
stunts.text: During a Shoot attack, spend a fate point and declare a specific condition you want to inflict on a target, like Shot in the Hand. If you succeed, you place that as a situation aspect on them in addition to hitting them for stress.

stunts.name: Master of the Lasso
stunts.text: +2 to create advantages with Shoot whenever this involves throwing a lasso.

stunts.name: Ranged Knockback
stunts.text: When you succeed with style on a Shoot attack with a thrown weapon, you may choose to reduce the value of your hit by one in order to move your opponent one zone, provided there are no situation aspects impeding this movement.

stunts.name: Subtle Draw
stunts.text: +2 to Shoot whenever there is active opposition to your first shot in a scene.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.15.3

stunts.name: Trained As a Unit/Team Player
stunts.text: You were trained alongside the rest of your unit, and now that unit is like a single organism. +2 to create advantages with Shoot whenever working with another character who is from the same unit as you and who also has this stunt. (A similar stunt could exist in many other skills.)

stunts.name: Two Gun Joe
stunts.text: Normally, shooting with two guns just looks cool, but when you fire two weapons, you have a decisive advantage. Any time you succeed on an attack with two guns, the stress inflicted is increased by one.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.15.4

stunts.name: Volley
stunts.text: When you combine Shoot skills with your allies, you contribute an additional +1 bonus.

stunts.name: Face in the Crowd
stunts.text: +2 to any Stealth roll to blend into a crowd. What a “crowd” means will depend on the environment—a subway station requires more people to be crowded than a small bar.

stunts.name: Gently Does It
stunts.text: Your Stealth skill works impeded by inanimate objects that will make sound if disturbed, such as brittle twigs, mouse traps, or wobbly piles of crates.

stunts.name: Slip Between the Shadows
stunts.text: +2 to create advantage or overcome with Stealth whenever you are in near-darkness or total darkness.

stunts.name: Stowaway
stunts.text: +2 to Stealth when hiding on a ship or other large vehicle.

stunts.name: Cunning Evasion
stunts.text: Once per scene, when you successfully defend against an area attack with Athletics, you may roll to create an advantage with Stealth as a free action.

stunts.name: Hidden Sniper
stunts.text: Once per scene, after you make a Shoot attack, you may roll to create advantage with Stealth as a free action.

stunts.name: Only the Wind Will See Me Go
stunts.text: At the cost of a fate point, you may exit a scene, passing from sight.

stunts.name: Quick Exit
stunts.text: A momentary distraction is all you need to vanish from the scene. Provided you are not in the midst of a conflict, you may roll a quick contest between your Stealth and the highest Notice in the room. If you succeed, the next time someone turns to look at or talk to you, you’re not there.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.27.2

stunts.name: Backstab/Sucker Punch
stunts.text: You can use Stealth to make physical attacks, provided your target isn’t already aware of your presence.

stunts.name: Backstab
stunts.text: When you can surprise an enemy or attack from a place of hiding, you can attack with Stealth. If you succeed, you create a boost. If you succeed with style, you get to invoke that boost for free twice.

stunts.name: In Plain Sight
stunts.text: You can use Stealth to hide even when you're out in the open and wouldn’t normally be able to justify it. However, as soon as you move, you become visible again, unless another stunt you have states otherwise.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.27.1

stunts.name: Ninja Vanish
stunts.text: Once per scene, you can vanish while in plain sight by spending a fate point, using a smoke pellet or other mysterious technique. This places the Vanished boost on you. While you’re vanished, no one can attack or create an advantage on you until after they’ve succeeded at an overcome roll with Notice to suss out where you went (basically meaning they have to give up an exchange to try). This aspect goes away as soon as you invoke it, or someone makes that overcome roll.

stunts.name: Shadowed Strike
stunts.text: After you invoke Vanished on an attack, you may defend with Stealth for the remainder of the current exchange.
stunts.requires: Master of Shadows and Ninja Vanish
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.27.1

stunts.name: Slippery Target
stunts.text: Provided you’re in darkness or shadow, you can use Stealth to defend against Shoot attacks from enemies that are at least one zone away.

stunts.name: Stalker
stunts.text: You like to watch people who don't know they're being watched. You may use Stealth in place of Investigate to conduct surveillance.

stunts.name: Hush
stunts.text: Your talent with stealth may be extended to others who are with you close by, provided that you travel as a group. As long as the whole group stays with you and follows your hushed orders, you may make a single Stealth roll for the whole group, using your skill alone. (You cannot apply the benefits of other stunts to this roll.) If someone breaks from the group, they immediately lose the benefits, and may risk revealing the rest of you if they don’t manage to pull off a little Stealth of their own. The maximum number of people that can be with you in the group is equal to your Stealth skill rating.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.27.3

stunts.name: Lightfoot
stunts.text: It’s difficult to track you when you take care to walk lightly. +2 to Stealth when overcoming traps based on weight or pressure.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.27.3

stunts.name: Master of Shadows
stunts.text: After you use In Plain Sight, you may move one zone per exchange without becoming visible. If there is an aspect in play that would normally justify the use of Stealth to hide, you may pay a fate point to be able to make an overcome action with Athletics without becoming visible.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.27.1

stunts.name: Not a Threat
stunts.text: Choose Deceive or Stealth when you take this stunt. When you create an advantage with that skill to make yourself as non-threatening or unobtrusive as possible, enemies will find other targets for as long as that aspect exists. As soon as you successfully attack someone, the aspect goes away.

stunts.name: Silent Tank
stunts.text: For some strange reason, you are capable of sneaking around while wearing 30 pounds of steel plating. You never suffer increased difficulty on Stealth rolls from being armoured.

stunts.name: Fierce Mind
stunts.text: +2 to overcome fear with Will.

stunts.name: Fighting For What You Believe In
stunts.text: Your faith, in someone or something, is absolute. Pick a being or a concept. +2 to Will when defending that thing or when overcoming separation from it.

stunts.name: Gift of Faith
stunts.text: +2 to defend with Will against fear and despair.

stunts.name: Indomitable/Fearless
stunts.text: +2 to defend against Provoke attacks specifically related to intimidation and fear.

stunts.name: Inner Strength
stunts.text: +2 to defend with Will against someone trying to get inside your head – be it through psychic means or through extensive torture.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.23.2

stunts.name: Mind of Steel
stunts.text: Magical mental influence is useless against your fortress-like mind! +2 to Will when using it to defend against supernatural mental attacks.

stunts.name: Set In My Ways
stunts.text: You're old. It took you decades to form your beliefs and you're not about to abandon them. Add +2 to your Will when using it to resist attempts to change your deeply-held beliefs or your core identity.

stunts.name: Stubborn Faith
stunts.text: You cling to your beliefs with amazing determination. +2 to Will when overcoming or defending against attempts to make you act directly against the principles of your faith.

stunts.name: Trust In My Leader
stunts.text: Pick a person or being who has authority over you and whom you trust. You gain +2 to Will whenever you resist attempts to undermine that trust.

stunts.name: Aplomb
stunts.text: When you go to check off a mental stress box and that box is already checked, you can check off the next lowest value empty box. If there are no unchecked boxes of a lower value, check off a higher value box as normal.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.23.1

stunts.name: Cool Customer
stunts.text: You are so at ease in times of mental stress that nothing seems to dent your calm regard of the situation. During a conflict, you may use your action to roll your Resolve against a target of Mediocre. If you succeed, you may either erase a check in your 1-point mental stress box or spend a fate point to erase a check from any single mental stress box with a value equal to or less than the shifts you gained on your roll.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.23.1

stunts.name: Driven
stunts.text: Whenever you take a moderate or severe consequence from a mental attack, you gain a free invocation on that consequence.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.23.2

stunts.name: Hard Boiled
stunts.text: You can choose to ignore a mild or moderate consequence for the duration of the scene. It can’t be compelled against you or invoked by your enemies. At the end of the scene it comes back worse, though; if it was a mild consequence it becomes a moderate consequence, and if it was already moderate, it becomes severe.

stunts.name: Never Broken
stunts.text: You gain a -8 physical consequence which recovers in the same way a -2 consequence does.

stunts.name: Smooth Recovery/Still Standing/Stubborn
stunts.text: You simply do not know when to quit. You gain an additional mild consequence slot. This slot can only be used for mental harm.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.23.2

stunts.name: Unyielding
stunts.text: Your force of will is enough to keep you going in the direst of circumstances. Each time you take physical stress, you may spend a fate point to instead take two 1-shift hits of mental stress.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.23.2

stunts.name: Determinate
stunts.text: Your astonishing determination allows you to push yourself beyond your physical limits. Use Will instead of Physique on any overcome rolls representing feats of endurance.

stunts.name: I'll Just Ignore You
stunts.text: Counterarguments are a waste of time. You prefer to simply not listen to the people you disagree with. You may use Will instead of Rapport to defend against attempts to damage your reputation or make you look bad in front of others.

stunts.name: Right Place, Right Time
stunts.text: You seem to always be in a safe spot, without moving in any obvious way. You may use Will to defend against physical attacks, and may also use it to move or take cover (so long as you merely saunter; no sprints allowed). To the outside world, it appears that you are simply staying put and unfazed as gunfire and other attacks miss you by scant inches, or are picking up your undisturbed martini as the werewolf rushes past. Circumstance conspires to leave you undisturbed so long as your defense is not beaten.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.23.1

stunts.name: Strength From Determination
stunts.text: Use Will instead of Physique on any overcome rolls representing feats of strength.

stunts.name: Sunday School
stunts.text: Your steadfastness comes from your religious upbringing. You may roll Will instead of Lore whenever seeking or recalling religious knowledge.

stunts.name: Unbroken Composure
stunts.text: Your mental strength allows you to remain calm when others would be caught off guard. You may use Will in place of Notice whenever someone is attempting to surprise you.

stunts.name: Extraordinary Concentration
stunts.text: Once per scene, when you successfully create an advantage with Will based on concentration, you gain one additional free invocation.

stunts.name: Iron Determination
stunts.text: You may, when you bluntly speak your true intentions in a social interaction, immediately gain a +1 bonus on all subsequent Provoke or Will rolls in that scene. However, if you do this, you may no longer use Rapport with the same audience, as you have peeled away the façade of civility.
stunts.source: adapted from Spirit of the Century SRD, §6.23.2

stunts.name: Laser-Like Focus
stunts.text: You find it easy to clear your mind in a stressful situation. +2 to create an advantage with Will related to concentration, willpower, or clear thought.

stunts.name: The Mind Is the Greatest Mountain
stunts.text: So far as social skills are concerned, you do not exist. You cannot be swayed, befriended, intimidated, or otherwise moved. Your speech reveals nothing about you or the veracity of your words. (If another character has the stunt The Inner Eye Sees Inner Truth, for the purposes of that stunt, your Deceive score is higher than their Empathy.)

stunts.name: Parrot
stunts.text: You can perfectly repeat anything you’ve heard in the last hour or so, even if you don’t know the language it was spoken in. (Normally a Will roll would be required to recall the words correctly.)
